title: Argentina name two SVNS debutants in star-studded squad
article_text:
Two potential HSBC SVNS Series debutants have been included in Argentina’s squad for Dubai and Cape Town, with Santiago Alvarez and Luciano Gonzalez the most experienced members of a squad that has played 389 events between them.

La Plata-product Luca Julian is set to wear a Los Pumas Sevens jersey for the first time, while Francisco Calello is also set for a maiden appearance on the SVNS Series. Calello did get to play for the national sevens team at the recent South American Championship in Cordoba.

Alvarez is the most-experienced player in the Los Pumas Sevens squad, with the forward set to earn his 79th tournament cap. Gonzalez has featured in 72 SVNS events, while Santiago Mare and Marcos Moneta have played at least 42 tournaments each.

Moneta was the top try-scorer on the SVNS Series last season, while Gonzalez earned Dream Team honours after another exceptional season. Argentina didn’t win any titles last season but did claim silver twice, and bronze another two times.

Argentina have been drawn in Pool A along with two-time reigning SVNS World Championship winners South Africa, Australia, and the United States. Los Pumas Sevens get their new campaign underway against the Blitzboks at 4:52 am on Saturday morning (Argentine time).

title: Beauden Barrett nears Bristol move as a two-year deal could make him the Gallagher PREM's top earner
article_text:
Beauden Barrett is in advanced talks to sign for Bristol Bears, according to reports on 24 November 2026.

The All Blacks fly-half and full-back just hit 150 test matches for New Zealand in their heavy defeat to England in the Rugby Nations Championship at Allianz Twickenham last weekend.

Read more: When will Beauden Barrett break the All Blacks test cap record?

A deal for Barrett to join Bristol is close to completion, according to the person posting, who says they were told this.

Bristol’s formal offer is with Barrett’s management, and the club are waiting for confirmation, according to Daily Mail. The deal is rumoured to be worth more than £1 million per season for two years, and it could also make him the highest-paid player in the Gallagher PREM.

All Black sabbaticals after a World Cup or early in a World Cup cycle are common with many opting for Japan, the Top 14 in France or Leinster.

The 2015 World Cup winner only has to look to his brother Jordie for the benefits of a sabbatical with the centre having played the 2024-25 season at Leinster, where he was then able to catapult towards some of his best rugby afterwards.

Newcastle Red Bulls have already turned down the chance to sign Barrett, the New Zealander, according to Ruck. Bristol reportedly face competition for Barrett from an unnamed French Top 14 club, according to Ruck.

title: Cowan-Dickie insists England will not let up after record triumph over All Blacks
article_text:
Luke Cowan-Dickie is adamant England will not let complacency creep in after their record win over the All Blacks, insisting they will not repeat the mistakes of the 2019 World Cup.

Cowan-Dickie is one of three players, with Jamie George and Maro Itoje, who would claim a fourth career win for England against New Zealand on Saturday if Steve Borthwick’s side back up last weekend’s 37-12 victory at Twickenham. The Sale hooker was part of the squad who defeated the All Blacks in the 2019 World Cup semi-final in emphatic fashion and went into the final against South Africa as favourites. Eddie Jones’s side were comfortably outplayed by the Springboks, however, with Cowan-Dickie acknowledging that England failed to hit their emotional peak that day.

Last weekend England flew out of the blocks, inspired by having Lewis Moody at the point of their V-formation response to the haka, and Cowan-Dickie is convinced there will be no complacency against the wounded All Blacks. Borthwick gave the players Monday off before resuming training on Tuesday.

Cowan-Dickie said: “Back then was the semi-final of the World Cup, maybe we left too much emotion out there and didn’t take enough into the final? Could we learn anything from that? Maybe little parts, complacency? Maybe that’s a big one. But the way we trained today, I don’t see any complacency. The boys are as up for it as they were last week.

“It’s a difficult one, I don’t know if we were complacent, it’s just the amount of emotion that went into that semi-final game, did we build the emotions back up for that final? The team we’ve got now is completely different. There are a lot of younger boys involved and they’re frothing at the bit. Obviously Lewis last week added that little bit but, for me, it’s a Test match. If we were playing tomorrow I’d be ready to go.”

Meanwhile, England’s wing sensation Will Joseph has revealed he has been receiving advice from his elder brother, Jonathan – who won 54 caps for his country – after proving Borthwick’s find of the autumn. Joseph won his first cap in 2022 but had to wait four years for a second, in which he scored a record-equalling five tries, earlier this month.

“It’s definitely been a whirlwind, it’s been pretty surreal. I’m quite literally pinching myself,” he said. “It’s very useful having [Jonathan]. I feel like everything I’m going through or experiencing, he definitely would have experienced. He also knows the game inside out, so he’s very supportive. He tells me bits he sees in my game and stuff I can improve on so he’s very useful to have as a brother.”

title: Syed Modi India International: Treesa-Gayatri pair enters quarterfinals
article_text:
LUCKNOW: Defending champions Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand advanced to the women’s doubles quarterfinals with a straight-games win while second seed Tanvi Sharma rallied from a game down to reach the women’s singles quarterfinals at the Syed Modi India International Super 300 on Thursday.

Treesa and Gayatri beat Shreya Balaji and Pranavi Natarajan 21-9, 21-8. Tanvi beat Indonesia’s Mutiara Ayu Puspitasari 18-21, 21-18, 21-18 in 68 minutes.

Unnati Hooda defeated American Ishika Jaiswal 21-14, 21-18 while Tasnim Mir upset Scotland’s sixth seed Kirsty Gilmour 21-19, 21-15.

Anmol Kharb completed the Indian women’s singles quartet by beating compatriot and fifth seed Ashmita Chaliha 21-16, 2115.

“I don’t think I played my best today,” Tanvi said. India’s Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto, the mixed doubles top seeds, lost 20-22, 15-21 to Malaysia’s Wee Yee Hern and Vannee Gobi.

Viraj Kuvale and Rutaparna Panda came from behind to win their mixed doubles match against Gregoire Deschamp and Iben Bergstein 16-21, 21-13, 21-17.

Sathwik Reddy Kanapuram and Reshika Uthayasooriyan also progressed In men’s singles, Tushar Suveer beat qualifier Shashwat Dalal 21-14, 21-12. Third seeds Hariharan Amsakarunan and MR Arjun advanced in men’s doubles.

title: An Se-young Takes Second Seed Despite 11 Season Wins at BWF Finals
article_text:
[OSEN=Seo Jeong-hwan Reporter] 'The world’s strongest with 11 season wins, yet a second seed...'

An Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance) was given the second seed at the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Finals, yielding the top seed to Japan’s Akane Yamaguchi.

The BWF announced on November 24 (Korean time) the list of participants for the 2026 World Tour Finals, scheduled to take place in Hangzhou, China, from December 9 to 13. In the women’s singles, world No. 1 An Se-young received the second seed, while world No. 2 Yamaguchi was awarded the first seed.

Why did An Se-young, who achieved 11 season wins, drop to the second seed? The seed allocation is based on the World Tour rankings, not the world rankings. It is a system that combines performance and ranking points accumulated in World Tour events during the season. Major tournaments such as the World Championships, Asian Championships, and Asian Games are not included in the World Tour rankings.

An Se-young dominated this season by winning all three major tournaments: the World Championships, Asian Championships, and Asian Games. However, she withdrew during the Japan Open and did not participate in the China Open. Due to reasons such as injury and conditioning management, An Se-young adjusted her tournament schedule, causing her World Tour ranking points to fall to second place.

In contrast, Yamaguchi consistently accumulated points by participating in 13 tournaments this season. As a result, she overtook An Se-young in the World Tour rankings and secured the first seed for this championship.

However, this does not necessarily mean an unfavorable draw for An Se-young. The first and second seeds are placed in separate brackets, and if both players reach the final, they will face each other. For An Se-young, avoiding Yamaguchi until the final could present an opportunity to win the title.

Ultimately, the winner will be An Se-young. The draw holds little significance. This World Tour Finals is a stage to determine the season’s strongest player. Eight players, including the top seven in the World Tour rankings and the World Championships winner, will compete for a total prize of 3 million dollars (approximately 4 billion Korean won).

An Se-young also has the chance to write a new history in badminton. Having already recorded 11 wins this season, she will surpass Japan’s Kento Momota’s record for the most single-season wins and become the first to achieve 12 wins if she claims victory.

Currently on a 55-match winning streak, An Se-young is also challenging Susi Susanti’s record of 59 consecutive wins in women’s singles. If she achieves an undefeated run at the World Tour Finals, she could set a historic 60-match winning streak.

Although she must settle for the second seed despite her 11 season wins, An Se-young’s goal is not seed ranking. Attention is focused on whether she can leave a new record in badminton history alongside the championship trophy in Hangzhou. / jasonseo34@osen.co.kr

title: Ahn Se-young targets 12th title and winning streak record at World Tour Finals
article_text:
"The world's best with 11 titles this season, yet only the No. 2 seed ..."

Ahn Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance) lost the top seed to Japan's Akane Yamaguchi at the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Finals.

The BWF announced on the 24th, Korea time, the list of players competing in the 2026 World Tour Finals, which will be held in Hangzhou, China, from Dec. 9-13. In women's singles, world No. 1 Ahn Se-young received the No. 2 seed, while world No. 2 Yamaguchi was given the top seed.

Why was Ahn Se-young, who has won 11 titles this season, pushed down to the No. 2 seed? Seeding is based on World Tour rankings, not world rankings. Players are ranked according to their results and ranking points earned at World Tour events over the course of a season. Results at major events such as the world championships, Asian championships and Asian Games are not included in the World Tour rankings.

Ahn Se-young had an outstanding season, winning the world championships, Asian championships and Asian Games. But on the World Tour, she withdrew during the Japan Open and did not compete at the China Open. Managing her schedule because of injuries and her condition, Ahn fell to No. 2 in the World Tour rankings.

Yamaguchi, by contrast, competed in as many as 13 tournaments this season and steadily accumulated points. She eventually overtook Ahn Se-young in the World Tour rankings and claimed the No. 1 seed at the season-ending championships.

That does not mean Ahn Se-young is guaranteed a tougher draw. The No. 1 and No. 2 seeds are placed in separate halves of the draw and cannot meet before the final. If both players reach the final, they will face each other then. For Ahn, not having to play Yamaguchi before the final could instead be an opportunity to win the title.

Ahn Se-young is bound to win anyway. The draw does not matter much. The World Tour Finals determine the season's top player. Eight players will compete for a total prize pool of $3 million (about 4 billion won): the top seven in the World Tour rankings and the world champion.

Ahn Se-young also has a chance to make badminton history at the tournament. She has already won 11 titles this season. If she wins the event, she will surpass the single-season record held by Japan's Kento Momota and become the first player ever to win 12 titles in a season.

Ahn Se-young, who is currently on a 55-match winning streak, is also chasing the women's singles record of 59 straight wins held by Susi Susanti. If she wins every match at the World Tour Finals, she could extend her streak to a historic 60 victories.

Although she must settle for the No. 2 seed despite winning 11 titles this season, Ahn Se-young's goal is not her seeding. All eyes will be on whether she can lift the trophy in Hangzhou and set a new record in world badminton history.

title: AITA election results to be kept in ‘sealed cover’
article_text:
on Thursday ordered that the results of the All India Tennis Association (AITA) elections scheduled for Friday should not be declared but kept under “sealed cover” until further orders The court came close to staying the elections altogether, with the two-judge bench of acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma displeased by the “conduct” of AITA and its counsel during the hearing.

It ultimately allowed the polls to proceed and posted the case for hearing on Dec 14.

The development assumes significance since World Tennis, formerly the International Tennis Federation (ITF), had earlier said that if AITA were to remain under the administrator’s supervision, the global body would consider suspending AITA’s membership.

title: Maincast Sport secures exclusive WTA rights in Ukraine from 2027
article_text:
Maincast Sport will become the exclusive home of WTA tennis in Ukraine starting in 2027. The channel has signed a long-term deal with the Women’s Tennis Association covering WTA 1000, WTA 500 and WTA 250 events, plus the season-ending WTA Finals, Maincast said.

The 2027 season will visit 26 countries and territories. It opens in January in Brisbane and Auckland, then moves through Indian Wells, Miami, Madrid, Rome and Beijing. The season wraps up in November with the FAGE WTA Finals in Charlotte, North Carolina, where the year’s top eight singles players and top eight doubles teams will compete.

Channel owner Maksym Krippa said the growing rights lineup is meant to let Ukrainian fans watch the world’s best competitions in Ukrainian. The WTA partnership, in his words, will let the channel show almost the entire women’s tennis season, including matches featuring Ukraine’s leading players, and bring new viewers to the sport.

Maincast co-founder Vitalii Volochai promised that matches featuring Elina Svitolina, Marta Kostyuk, Dayana Yastremska and other Ukrainian players will air exclusively on Maincast Sport. Alongside live coverage, the channel is preparing its own shows, analysis programs and broadcasts with star guests. “The WTA is an almost year-round tournament cycle, so Maincast Sport viewers will get top-level tennis every week,” Volochai added.

WTA Ventures, the association’s commercial arm, also commented on the deal. Its CEO Marina Storti said the partnership will bring more women’s tennis to fans in Ukraine. She also noted that Ukrainian players continue to make a notable impact on the global game.

WTA matches will air on the Maincast Sport channel and stream on the Maincast.tv platform. In late October, Maincast launched an app for Maincast.tv on Android TV devices. Beyond the WTA Tour, Maincast Sport holds broadcast rights to the NBA, Spain’s Copa del Rey, MotoGP and NASCAR.

title: Spain captain reveals when Carlos Alcaraz will play at the Davis Cup after he misses opening tie
article_text:
Spain captain David Ferrer has revealed why Carlos Alcaraz sat out his side’s opening tie at the Davis Cup, as he toasted a victory for his side against Austria.

Alcaraz’s participation at the biggest team event in men’s tennis was in real doubt after he underwent a scan on a damaged hamstring at last week’s ATP Finals in Turin.

While he went on to win the end-of-season finals with a victory against world No 1 Alexander Zverev in the final, Alcaraz admitted he would assess his fitness before committing to playing at the Davis Cup.

“The Davis Cup is something very important to me,” he said after the win against Zverev last Sunday.

“I’ll try to get to Bologna as ready as possible physically. It’s going to be a very, very nice week, and one I’m really looking forward to.”

Plenty of medical experts would have voiced their concern over Alcaraz playing at the Davis Cup and Spain captain Ferrer took the cautious approach as he left his star man out of the team for their quarter-final against Austria.

Despite Alcaraz’s absence, Spain still found a way to get through to a semi-final showdown with Great Britain as Daniel Merida and Rafael Jodar secured wins against Joel Schwaerzler and Jurij Rodionov to seal victory in the tie.

Afterwards, Ferrer revealed Alcaraz is expected to return to action when the semi-final tie is contested.

“We didn’t want to take any risks with the physical problem Carlos was dealing with,” said Ferrer. “And I’m very happy because Carlos will be ready this weekend. He will be ready for Saturday.”

Ferrer went on to salute his two singles winners, as he reserved special praise for world No 39 Daniel Merida.

“Dani Mérida is a pleasant surprise,” he added. “He’s handling it calmly and that isn’t easy considering he’s only making his Davis Cup debut this year

“Winning the first set was crucial because, whether you like it or not, he started nervously, and the other player had break points. But I think once he won the first set, he shook off those nerves and felt very comfortable in the second.

“It’s also true that Rodionov started playing very well, very well tactically and with nothing to lose. He struggled to find his rhythm at the beginning.

“In the second set, I tried to reassure him (Jodar) that everything was fine, that we needed to play long rallies so he could find his timing, and that’s what happened.

“When he started playing longer rallies and Rodionov began to take more risks and had to play more aggressively, the dynamic of the match changed.”

Alcaraz has suggested winning the Davis Cup is one of the big targets in his career, despite the fact the tournament has lost its importance in the tennis calendar in recent years.

If he wins two singles matches over the weekend, Alcaraz may tick off the Davis Cup on his record and after that, he may not need to play in the event in the future.

title: Jodar, Merida fire Spain into Davis Cup SFs as Alcaraz watches on
Cost of Jannik Sinner’s extended injury lay-off revealed as he misses out on a huge cash windfall
article_text:
Jannik Sinner is set to miss another few months of action after confirming he has undergone surgery on the knee injury that has kept him off court since he won the Wimbledon title last July.

Sinner has made a few aborted attempts to return to the court over the last few months, but he finally accepted he needed to go under the knife in a decision that will see him miss the Australian Open in January.

There is no confirmed timescale on Sinner’s comeback, but this latest setback has already proved costly for the world No 2, as he is set to miss out on a chance to challenge for millions of dollars in prize money over the next few months.

His ranking will also suffer as he spends more time recovering from surgery and after such a long lay-off, he will also face the prospect of working his way back to top form when he returns.

Here is your Tennis365 guide to the financial cost of Sinner’s injury so far and how much it will cost him heading into 2027.

After being absent for the last six months since Wimbledon, Sinner has already missed out on as must as $10m of prize money.

The $5m jackpot on offer for the US Open champion was collected by Alexander Zverev, but Sinner would have been a strong favourite to beat him to that title if he was fit, given his recent record against the newly crowned world No 1.

Sinner could also have expected to collect millions of dollars by playing in the Cincinnati Masters in August, as well as throughout the Asian swing of the tour and then the lucrative indoor season.

Alcaraz went on a stunning run of success as he lifted titles in Tokyo, Vienna in ATP 500 events, where he would also have collected a hefty appearance fee.

On top of that, Sinner then missed out on a potential $5m windfall at the ATP Finals in Turin, with Alcaraz picking up $5,171,000 for his win in Italy.

Since returning to action at the US Open, Alcaraz has collected an eye-watering $8.13m in prize money and Sinner could have expected to collect a similar haul if he was active over the last few months.

The confirmation that Sinner is out of the Australian Open ensured he will also miss the Six Kings Slam in Saudi Arabia next month.

That means he will not collect the guaranteed $1.5m appearance fee for playing in the exhibition event, with the cost of his absence certain to escalate in the months that follow.

Sinner won $4.34m in prize money between January and early April this year and he is set to miss out on a chance to repeat that run of success in the opening months of 2027.

If his absence was to extend beyond the French Open and Wimbledon, he would be losing the chance to challenge for huge prize money in a lucrative phase of the tennis season.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Sinner will be guaranteed bonus payments from his sponsors for big tournament success and they are out of reach when he out with an injury.

Nike, Gucci, Rolex, HEAD, Lavazza and Allianz Insurance are among Sinner’s backers and while they will still be paying his handsomely to be part of his story, but the bonus payments will the on hold until returns to court.

Sinner will also miss out on big handouts from the ATP Bonus Pool, as players are downgraded if they miss events and Sinners looks set to miss the Indian Wells and Miami Open tournaments in March, as well as the Monte Carlo Masters. He won all three of those tournaments in 2026.

Sinner does not return until mid-April or May, the full cost of his absence could be as much as $15m and that figure can be enhanced by the absence of appearance fees and bonus payments from sponsors and the ATP Tour.

Of course, Sinner’s cash blow will not have a big impact on him as he has already won $70,675,661 in his career before sponsorship and bonus payments are added to that total.

title: Daniil Medvedev sets unwanted ATP record for 2026 after playing his final event of the season in Turin
GB win doubles decider to reach Davis Cup semi-finals for first time since 2019
article_text:
Great Britain advanced to the semi-finals of the Davis Cup for the first time since 2019 as Henry Patten and Neal Skupski won a decisive doubles tie against third seeds Germany in Bologna.

Patten and Skupski, playing together for the first time since announcing their doubles partnership for the 2027 season, proved too clinical for Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz.

They converted two break points and saved five in the first set, before overturning a mini-break in the tie-break to win 6-2 7-6 (8-6).

Skupski was involved in a Davis Cup quarter-final loss playing alongside Joe Salisbury against the same German doubles pair in December 2021 - a defeat that was in his mind as Thursday's decider progressed.

"I thought about that match during the match today and I was determined not to let that happen again," Skupski told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"No matter what was happening today, we weren't going to come off the court very easily with a loss."

World number one Alexander Zverev had earlier sent the tie to its full distance by defeating British number one Arthur Fery in straight sets to cancel out Cameron Norrie's three-set victory over Jan-Lennard Struff.

Great Britain's semi-final is scheduled for Saturday and Leon Smith's team will discover their next opponents later on Thursday when Spain meet Austria in the last of the four quarter-finals.

Defending champions Italy will play Czech Republic in Friday's first semi-final.

Smith will step down as captain at the end of the tournament and Great Britain retain hopes of a second victory under his leadership, following the most recent of their 10 Davis Cup successes in 2015.

"I felt the same sort of pressure, nerves and butterflies beforehand and during the matches," said Smith, who has been captain since 2010.

"You sit for a long time in that chair on your own on a day like this, a lot of thoughts go through your head and one of the things I kept reminding myself is how much of a privilege it is to be in this situation.

"I loved it but, more importantly, I'm thrilled for the guys. They've committed so well to this, they've been to a few different places over the past 18 months to get to this opportunity and I'm delighted they've got to the final four now."

World number 52 Norrie had got Great Britain off to the perfect start with a three-set win against Struff, a player 13 places above him in the world rankings.

The left-hander raced through the first set in just 23 minutes but a break late in the second set by Struff forced a decider.

The key moment came at 2-2 in the final set when Norrie saved four break points to hold serve, after which he won 12 of the next 14 points to complete a 6-3 3-6 6-2 victory.

Norrie's success meant a win for Fery against Zverev, a two-time major champion in 2026, would have been enough to secure Great Britain's passage through to the last four.

However, as he did in their Wimbledon semi-final in July, Zverev proved too strong for 24-year-old Fery and ended as a 6-3 6-2 winner.

Patten and Skupski have found themselves unusually in the spotlight over the past week following the former's "ruthless" split from Harri Heliovaara in favour of joining forces with his compatriot next season.

While their partnership is in its infancy, there were few signs of teething problems as they extended their Davis Cup record as a pair to 3-0.

Patten's pinpoint returns and sharp reactions at the net coupled with Skupski's impressive serving proved too strong for Krawietz and Puetz, who were left to rue missed opportunities.

In a sticky opening service game, Patten double-faulted on the opening point and faced a break point, while Skupski saved four in game seven of the opening set.

Neither pair earned a break point in the second set, with the British duo dropping just five points on serve.

Trailing 3-1 in what turned out to be a thrilling tie-break, they fought back to lead 6-5 before closing out the win at the second opportunity.

"It doesn't feel like the end of the season for those two because they've just paired up," Smith said. "There's been a buoyancy in their practice sessions because it's a new start.

"They were brilliant today. You don't know if you're going to get a match or not [as doubles players] but I saw them 20 minutes before their match and you could just see they were delighted to get this opportunity and that gave them a huge lift."

title: BWF revamps major badminton championships, introduces new formats from 2027
article_text:
BEIJING, Nov 26 — The Badminton World Federation has approved sweeping changes to the formats of its major championships, expanding its flagship team competitions to 24 teams and introducing a group stage at the individual World Championships from 2027, Xinhua reported.

The Thomas and Uber Cups, badminton’s men’s and women’s world team championships, will also switch from best-of-five to best-of-three-match ties from 2028.

The Thomas and Uber Cups and the Sudirman Cup, the world mixed team championship, will adopt league stages followed by knockout rounds, replacing their existing group-stage formats.

Each team will play three league-stage ties at the Sudirman Cup, which will retain its best-of-five-match format, while teams at the Thomas and Uber Cups will each contest four ties.

Under a new points system, teams will earn one point for every individual match won, regardless of the overall result of the tie, with two bonus points awarded for a tie victory. The top 12 teams in each competition will advance to the knockout stage.

The system is designed to give greater significance to individual matches, even after the outcome of a tie has been decided.

From 2027, the individual World Championships will move from a straight knockout format to a group stage followed by knockout rounds across all five disciplines, bringing the competition closer to the format used at the Olympic Games.

The men’s and women’s singles events will each feature 48 players divided into 16 groups of three, while each of the three doubles events will feature 32 pairs across eight groups of four.

The format guarantees every player or pair at least two matches, with each national association permitted a maximum of four entries per event.

“These changes to our major championships are about creating stronger competition, opening the door to greater participation, and ensuring more members and players can share in badminton’s biggest moments,” BWF President Khunying Patama Leeswadtrakul said.

“Together with the introduction of the 3x15 scoring system, they form part of a broader vision to elevate our sport, deepen fan engagement, and strengthen badminton’s position as a truly global game.”

The BWF also confirmed several hosts for its major championships through 2030.

Mississauga, Canada, will stage the 2027 World Championships, while New Delhi will host the 2028 Thomas and Uber Cups. South Korea will stage the 2029 Sudirman Cup, with the host city yet to be determined, and Paris will host the 2030 Thomas and Uber Cups.

Beijing was announced last month as host of the 2027 Sudirman Cup. — Bernama-Xinhua

The 2026 field for the Next Gen ATP Finals is set
article_text:
Eight of the best 20-and-under players in men’s tennis will meet in Reggio Calabria from 9 to 13 December. A 17-year-old qualifier, a returning top seed and two home hopes lead a field made up mostly of debutants.

The line-up is complete. Czech teenager Jan Kumstat and Austria’s Joel Schwaerzler took the last two direct places on 23 November. They join Martin Landaluce, Moise Kouame, Rei Sakamoto, Federico Cina, Darwin Blanch and Italian wild card Pierluigi Basile.

The two biggest names of the 20-and-under generation will not be there. Race leader Rafael Jodar, who reached the Nitto ATP Finals in his first full year on tour and is now with Spain at the Davis Cup Final 8, will not take part. Joao Fonseca, the 2024 champion, is also out after ending his season through injury. Their absence leaves the title wide open and guarantees a first-time champion.

- Edition: 9th. The event returns to Italy, where it began in Milan in 2017, after three years in Jeddah.

- Defending champion: Learner Tien. He won in 2025 but is now too old to return.

- Who qualifies: The top seven players aged 20 or under (born in 2006 or later) in the PIF ATP Live Race To Reggio Calabria, which closed on 15 November, plus one wild card from the Italian federation (FITP).

- Format: Two round-robin groups of four. The top two in each group reach the semi-finals.

- Rules: Best-of-five sets, with each set played to four games, a tie-break at 3–3 and no-ad scoring. Hawk-Eye Live calls the lines, and players may talk to their coaches during matches.

The group draw has not been announced yet.

Seeds follow the final Race standings. Basile entered on the Italian federation’s wild card.

Landaluce is the only player in the field who has been here before, and he arrives as the top seed.

Kouame, 17, is the youngest player in the field and a debutant, actually the youngest qualifier in tournament history. French players who have appeared at the event include Hugo Gaston, Arthur Fils and Luca Van Assche.

Cina, 19, is one of two Italians in the field and will have home support in Reggio Calabria.

Blanch, 19, is a debutant from the United States. He won his first Challenger title in Tiburon in September.

Kumstat, 19, is a debutant from Czechia. He took one of the last two direct places on 23 November.

Schwaerzler, 20, is a debutant from Austria. He took the last direct place in the field.

Basile, 19, is the Italian wild card and a debutant.

Jodar and Fonseca had the two highest Race totals by a wide margin. Neither will play. Their absence moved Landaluce to the top seed and opened places for Kumstat and Schwaerzler. Felix Balshaw was next in the Race and missed out, along with Nicolai Budkov Kjaer and Diego Dedura.

title: AITA presidential election: Chintan Parekh vs Rohit Rajpal - two visions for Indian tennis
article_text:
NEW DELHI: The race for the All India Tennis Association (AITA) presidency pits Chintan Parekh's "Tennis First" motto against Rohit Rajpal's "The Next Serve," with both candidates promising to address Indian tennis' structural challenges.

While Parekh's pitch centres on governance reform, financial sustainability and expanding tennis beyond established centres; Rajpal has outlined a more programme-driven roadmap with specific proposals, timelines and targets. Their approaches differ on how to tackle key issues confronting Indian tennis.

Chintan Parekh wants to expand talent scouting beyond established centres, with a focus on underserved regions such as the North-East. His vision includes coaching pyramids and grooming young players for a stronger tennis ecosystem by 2030.

Rohit Rajpal proposes a state-wise development audit within 100 days, common talent-identification protocols, zonal camps, a central player database and low-cost talent scouting in underserved districts.

Chintan Parekh wants to take tennis to regions lacking infrastructure, particularly beyond metropolitan centres, and tap talent in remote and underserved areas.

Rohit Rajpal plans to expand national and zonal centres of excellence, partner state associations, develop infrastructure in the Northeast and hill regions, and explore a high-altitude training centre.

3. More tournaments at domestic and international level

Chintan Parekh focuses on strengthening AITA's finances to fund tennis development, but has not outlined specific targets for tournament expansion.

Rohit Rajpal wants to bring ATP and WTA events back to India, expand Challenger, ITF and junior tournaments, rotate events across zones, and build women's and senior circuits with at least 30 tournaments annually by 2030.

Chintan Parekh identifies better governance as the key pillar under his presidency. He promises transparent, player-centric governance and a clean-up of AITA's institutional structure. He wants the AITA Trust to be brought under the association's umbrella, its trustees restructured, and issues concerning AITA's relationship with Delhi Lawn Tennis Association (DLTA) resolved.

Rohit Rajpal proposes published accounts, budgets and fund utilisation, along with Athletes, Ethics and Dispute Resolution committees. He also promises transparent selection criteria, calendars and measurable progress reports.

5. How to make tennis financially viable

Chintan Parekh wants to build AITA's corpus to ₹200-250 crore over four years, tap CSR funding and create greater financial capacity to support budding players.

"Our vision is a very clean AITA with a focus on the players. Grassroots development is important so scholarships for talented children in rural areas(is one target).

Tennis is still considered an affluent sport, one for the elite. The first step is to clean it up (the corruption). The second step is to build the grassroots, then get the funding in, empower the state associations who empower the players,"

, who is the vice-presidential candidate in Parekh's team, had told select media after filing his nomination.

Rohit Rajpal proposes travel and tournament-entry assistance for professionals, a CSR-funded Players' Distress Fund and a feasibility study for a pension scheme for retired players.

Should AITA prioritize expanding tennis infrastructure in underserved regions?

Parekh's pitch is centred on institutional reform, financial strength and widening tennis' reach. Rajpal's manifesto offers a structured roadmap with programmes, timelines and measurable targets.

Both promise to address Indian tennis' longstanding challenges. The real test, however, will be turning those promises into tangible opportunities for players.

title: Alexander Zverev calls out ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi over ‘unfair’ remarks
article_text:
Alexander Zverev has described comments that ATP Tour chairman Andrea Gaudenzi made about players playing through pain as “unfair.”

At a press conference during the ATP Finals in Turin last week, Gaudenzi said current players are “smart” at managing injuries and suggested they use painkillers less often than his generation.

“I think I played the last seven years of my career with painkillers, and I broke my shoulder here in Milan in Davis Cup final because I took a cortisone injection six weeks before the final,” said the Italian, who played on the ATP Tour between 1990 and 2003.

“So we were really a little bit old style going and die on the court until you break.

“I think these guys today, first of all, they have smarter science behind, smarter teams, there is a lot of medical evolution, but they take prevention very seriously, rightly so, because they want to have a longer career, which is smarter.”

The former world No 18 added: “Hardly ever any of them plays when they have a potential injury coming up, which I think is the right thing to do, by the way.

“I think they’re very smart and should do that, rather than overplaying and chasing the money.”

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

At the Davis Cup Finals in Bologna, Zverev was asked about Gaudenzi’s claim and whether he has had to play through pain frequently in 2026.

“No, look, I think it’s an unfair comment from Gaudenzi because he doesn’t know how much painkillers we take. It’s not like every time we take a painkiller we let him know,” said the world No 1.

“Yeah, look, I think this year for me, it’s been a good year. I’ve said it before: I was much, much healthier this year than I was last year.

“Last year, I was struggling a lot with my back. I had a lot of bone issues, as well, which I luckily figured out where it came from and I could take the medication for it.

“But yeah, I think generally speaking, I felt good throughout the year. I think after the US Open, fatigue came in. I was more tired. I feel like I played a couple of tournaments not as good as I played before.

“I think I’ve played more tennis than anybody else. Taking that into consideration, I think I can be very happy with how this year went.

“Yeah, I look forward to next year. I look forward to finishing strong here. I really, really look forward to going on holidays and having a good start to the 2027 season.”

title: “Unfair comment” – Alexander Zverev Bluntly Calls Out ATP Chairman After ‘Painkiller’ Comment On Hectic Schedule Sparks Controversy
article_text:
Alexander Zverev took a jab at ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi over his comments about players' use of painkillers amid the demanding tennis schedule.

Gaudenzi recently claimed that modern players are better at managing their physical condition and depend less on painkillers than the players did when he competed. He also recalled relying on painkillers during the seven years of his career and added that players in the past often competed despite injuries. Gaudenzi's comments came amid growing concerns about the demanding tennis calendar and its increasing toll on players.

However, his opinions did not land well with Zverev, who, during the press conference ahead of the Davis Cup, called out Gaudenzi. The German tennis player stated that it was unfair of the ATP chairman because he had no idea how many painkillers players actually take. Zverev further mentioned that he was much healthier this year compared to last year, when he struggled with back and bone problems before finding the medication to manage them.

"No, look, I think it's an unfair comment from Gaudenzi because he doesn't know how much painkillers we take," Zverev said. "It's not like every time we take a painkiller we let him know. Yeah, look, I think this year for me, it's been a good year. I've said it before: I was much, much healthier this year than I was last year. Last year I was struggling a lot with my back. I had a lot of bone issues, as well, which I luckily figured out where it came from and I could take the medication for it."

Alexander Zverev will lead the German team at the 2026 Davis Cup.

In the same press conference, a reporter asked Alexander Zverev about his experience recovering from a serious injury and whether the German player was planning to contact the Italian ace, who underwent minor right knee surgery on Tuesday in Finland to treat his iliotibial band. Zverev reflected on his severe right ankle injury, which he sustained during his 2022 Roland Garros semi-final match against Rafael Nadal.

He added that the recovery kept him away from tennis for seven to eight months. Zverev mentioned that Sinner had initially hoped to return for the US Open and Asian swing. He also praised the five-time Grand Slam champion's mental strength and mentioned that they met in Turin, where he wished Sinner a speedy return.

"I think with my injury, it was very, very clear what happened," Zverev said. "It was very, very clear the path forward I had to take. I broke seven ligaments, had a few fractures in my bones. I knew exactly the path it would take. I knew from the start it would take me at least seven to eight months to come back. With Jannik, the big difference is that he was hoping on a weekly basis that he could come back. He was hoping for US Open. He was hoping for the Asia tour, so on. Now four or five months into the injury, he decided to take surgery."

"Again, I'm not a doctor. I'm not a medical expert. I don't know exactly what the recovery looks like for his type of injury. I think he's mentally strong. We know that he's mentally strong. I hope that he takes every step seriously and that in three, four months' time he can be back to 100% and be back playing. Even though of course he's one of my biggest competitors, one of the most difficult players for me to play, I still wish for him to come back to the tour because, as you said, I've been there, I know what injury feels like, and I don't wish injury upon anyone. I saw him in Turin and I texted him. I didn't speak to him on the phone."

Jannik Sinner's last competition was at the Wimbledon Championships, where he defeated Alexander Zverev in the final round.

title: Badminton: BWF switch Thomas-Uber Cup Finals to best-of-three format in major revamp
article_text:
PETALING JAYA: Marathon ties lasting more than five hours could soon be a thing of the past at the Thomas Cup Finals.

In a bid to make the sport more engaging for fans, the Badminton World Federation (BWF) have decided to move away from the traditional best-of-five format at the Thomas and Uber Cup Finals, with ties set to be decided by just three matches – two singles and one doubles – under a major revamp of the team competitions.

The Sudirman Cup will also undergo changes, but the mixed team competition will retain its best-of-five format.

Points-based system will be introduced at the 2028 Thomas and Uber Cup Finals in New Delhi.

A 3-0 victory will earn a team five points, while a 2-1 win will be worth four points. Teams losing 1-2 will still collect one point.

At the end of the group stage, the 12 best-performing teams will advance to the knockout stage.

BWF president Patama Leeswadtrakul said the changes were aimed at allowing more member associations to qualify for the championships while making the team competitions more exciting.

"The future of badminton depends on our ability to innovate, expand our reach and remain relevant to audiences around the world.

"These changes to our major championships are about creating stronger competition, opening the door to greater participation, and ensuring more members and players can share in badminton's biggest moments.

"Together with the introduction of the 3×15 scoring system, they form part of a broader vision to elevate our sport, deepen fan engagement, and strengthen badminton's position as a truly global game," said Patama.

The points allocation will differ for Sudirman Cup from April 21-May 2 in Beijing.

The 2027 edition will feature 24 teams, up from 16 previously, with the teams divided into three groups of eight.

The groupings are understood to be based on the teams' current rankings, marking a departure from the previous format, where 16 teams were drawn into four groups.

Meanwhile, the 2027 World Championships in Mississauga, Canada, will also adopt a format similar to that used at the Olympic Games, with a group stage followed by a knockout phase across all five disciplines.

The singles events will feature 48 players divided into 16 groups of three, while the doubles events will comprise 32 pairs split into eight groups of four.

The top two players or pairs from each group will advance to the round of 16.

title: BWF Syed Modi International 2026: Lee Zii Jia maintains title bid with straight-games last 16 victory in Lucknow
India To Host 2028 Thomas And Uber Cup Finals In New Delhi
article_text:
New Delhi will host the 2028 Thomas and Uber Cup Finals. See India's record in both cups, what BAI said, and whether the capital's venue is ready.

The Badminton World Federation (BWF) has awarded New Delhi the hosting rights for the 2028 Thomas and Uber Cup Finals, the men’s and women’s world teams championship. The Badminton Association of India (BAI) announced this on 25 November 2026, after successfully hosting the 2026 BWF World Championships in New Delhi in August. The World Championship held at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium welcomed more than 400 players from over 50 nations. The Thomas and Uber Cup is the third major BWF tournament that India has landed in three years, after the 2025 World Junior Championships in Guwahati. The 2028 finals return to India after 14 years, since 2014.

Commenting on the announcement, BAI President Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma said, “Over the past few years, we at BAI have worked to make India a partner the BWF can count on to stage its biggest events. China has played that role for many years, and India has now earned that same trust. Our players have raised India’s standing on court, winning the Thomas Cup in 2022 and taking bronze in 2026. As a federation, we have built the organisational capacity and mobilised the financial resources needed to deliver championships of this scale.”

“I thank Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji for his vision of making India a sought-after destination for the world’s biggest sporting events. By bringing championships like the Thomas & Uber Cup Finals to India, BAI is helping build the hosting track record that will strengthen the country’s bid to stage the Olympic Games. We will build on what we achieved in Guwahati and New Delhi, deliver a memorable Thomas & Uber Cup Finals in 2028 and continue to bring the biggest events in world badminton to India,” Dr. Sarma further added.

BAI Hony. General Secretary Shri Sanjay Mishra said, “Securing three of badminton’s biggest international championships for India in three years reflects the confidence the BWF has in our ability to deliver. It is a fitting way to close a year in which Indian shuttlers delivered strong results across formats, including a Thomas Cup bronze. When the Finals return to India after 14 years, our players will have the opportunity to compete for a world team title in front of a home crowd. Under the leadership of BAI President Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma, we set clear goals for Indian badminton, both on the court and as hosts of major international events. I am proud of what we have achieved together. My special thanks to Hon’ble Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya and the Sports Authority of India for their support, and to my colleagues at BAI, our players and support staff for their hard work. This is a collective achievement.”

India's men won the Thomas Cup once, in 2022, and took bronze this year at the edition in Horsens, Denmark. The women have two Uber Cup bronze medals. The first came on home soil in 2014, India's first Uber Cup medal, and the second followed two years later. This will be the second time India hosts the Finals, as New Delhi also staged the team events in 2014.

New Delhi's recent record suggests the answer is yes. The BWF World Championships were held at the Indira Gandhi Stadium, and athletes from many nations were accommodated successfully. The venue had enough courts, and the management of the event was good.

The stadium also went through a big upgrade before the Worlds, after pigeons disrupted the India Open. Organisers refurbished 2,500 seats, renovated 57 of its 66 toilets and installed double doors at 16 inner hall entrances to keep birds out. They covered ventilator openings and sealed broken windows, and improved air conditioning, lighting, cleanliness, security and entry arrangements. It was the tournament's return to India after 17 years, and its 30th edition overall. BAI officials said the revamped venue put the India Open problems behind it.

title: Rafael Nadal (40) returns on December 12 with 27 Spanish legends: 17 Roland Garros titles on one court
article_text:
Rafael Nadal will return to court on December 12 at his academy in Manacor, joining 27 other Spanish tennis figures for a team doubles event celebrating its tenth anniversary. December 12 will be his second court appearance since retiring, with a Las Vegas exhibition already booked for February 2027.

The Rafa Nadal Academy confirmed the event on Wednesday under the name “El Gran Encuentro del Tenis Español”. It follows the Academy Slam in October and gives the anniversary celebrations an all-Spanish identity.

The 28-player line-up brings together several eras of Spanish tennis. Sergi Bruguera, Roland Garros champion in 1993 and 1994, will take part alongside Albert Costa, who won in Paris in 2002. Together with Nadal’s record 14 titles, that puts 17 Roland Garros singles crowns on the same courts.

David Ferrer, now Spain’s Davis Cup captain, joins a strong group that also includes Feliciano López, Tommy Robredo, Nicolás Almagro and Roberto Bautista Agut. Carla Suárez Navarro and Anabel Medina represent the women’s game, while veterans José Higueras and Jordi Arrese bring the experience of an earlier generation.

The all-Spanish format gives the evening a different feel from October. Rather than a reunion of international rivals, it celebrates a period when Spain produced champions at a rate few countries have ever matched.

Nadal ended his professional career in November 2024, playing his final match for Spain at the Davis Cup Finals in Málaga. His next public appearance came at the Academy Slam on October 3, nearly two years later, where he led Team Rafa against a side captained by Andy Murray. Each match was decided by a super tiebreak, and Team Rafa won the day.

Since then, Nadal has gradually accepted more invitations, with each appearance framed as a celebration rather than a comeback, though the pleasure he takes in competing comes through clearly enough. “I have always loved competing, and even if my professional career is finished, that feeling never really goes away,” he said in October.

His next major outing is already confirmed. On February 28, 2027, Nadal will headline the MGM Slam Presented by Capital One at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, his first appearance on a hard court and his first in the United States since retiring. The event takes place just days before the start of the Indian Wells Masters.

“Now I return in a different stage of my life, without the pressure of the tour but with the same passion for this sport,” Nadal said when the event was announced in October. He played in Las Vegas in March 2024, facing Carlos Alcaraz in a sold-out exhibition streamed on Netflix. No further players or format details for the 2027 edition have been announced yet.

The December event also reflects how much the academy has grown. Nadal opened it in his hometown in October 2016, with Roger Federer attending the inauguration, and it has since become a training base for hundreds of young players from around the world.

Three appearances in roughly five months mark a steady return to court life. On December 12 the setting will be the most personal of all: home courts, familiar faces and the clay where his academy story began.

title: Breaking: Jeonju City Abandons 2029 Sudirman Cup Hosting Over Financial Woes
article_text:
[Sports Chosun Choi Man-sik Reporter] The hosting of the Sudirman Cup, a world-class international event, in South Korea is expected to end in a farce.

This is because Jeonju City in North Jeolla Province, which was selected as the host city for the Sudirman Cup, has declared its withdrawal from hosting the event.

The Badminton World Federation (BWF) announced on the night of the 25th (Korean time) that Jeonju City in North Jeolla Province, South Korea, had been chosen as the host for the 2029 World Mixed Team Championships.

The World Mixed Team Championships, launched in Jakarta, Indonesia, in 1989 and held biennially, is one of the most prestigious international tournaments alongside the Thomas Cup (World Men’s Team Championships), Uber Cup (World Women’s Team Championships), World Individual Championships, and All England Open.

The tournament is also called the Sudirman Cup to honor Dick Sudirman, a legend of Indonesian badminton and hailed as the "father of badminton," who contributed to its establishment when Indonesia was a badminton powerhouse.

The Korea Badminton Association has long aspired to host an international tournament. While it hosted the World Junior Championships in Incheon in 2006 and the World Senior Championships in 2023, it had never secured a top-tier elite international event.

The BWF’s announcement of Jeonju as the host seemed to resolve the Korean badminton community’s long-standing wish, but it has ended in a sad conclusion. After Sports Chosun’s report citing the BWF’s official announcement on the 26th, Jeonju City stated, “Due to financial circumstances, we have decided to withdraw from hosting the 2029 Sudirman Cup.”

According to Jeonju City and the Korea Badminton Association, the city submitted an expression of interest to host the 2029 event to the BWF in the first half of this year. The Korea Badminton Association then leveraged its sports diplomacy to secure the "Jeonju hosting" decision at the BWF board meeting late last month.

The BWF formally notified the Korea Badminton Association of this decision via an official letter a week ago. The association then informed Jeonju City, but the city sent a letter renouncing its commitment to host the event.

Jeonju City is currently promoting a complex sports town project near the Jeonju World Cup Stadium, but parts of it have been suspended due to recent financial issues. Although construction of the Jeonju Indoor Gymnasium, designated as the main venue for the Sudirman Cup, is ongoing, it is reportedly impossible to complete it by the 2029 tournament date.

This led Jeonju City to abandon its bid to host the Sudirman Cup. Choi Man-sik Reporter cms@sportschosun.com

As local Japanese media previewed the women's singles event at the Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Finals, the season-ending championship, they mentioned only "badminton queen" An Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance) among the overseas top contenders.

Japanese broadcaster TBS reported on the 25th (Korea time), "The BWF released its World Tour rankings on the 24th, finalizing the players who have secured qualification for the Finals."

In women's singles, world No. 2 Akane Yamaguchi (29) and Tomoka Miyazaki (20), known as the "badminton idol," each secured one spot. In this season's World Tour rankings, Yamaguchi stands at No. 1, while Miyazaki is ranked No. 5.

Another Japanese player, Nozomi Okuhara (31), also ranked No. 7 in the World Tour rankings, but her trip to Hangzhou was canceled as a maximum of two players per country or region can compete in women's singles.

The last time a Japanese player won the Finals was in 2022. Yamaguchi, who lifted the women's singles trophy at that time, is aiming to reclaim the top spot after four years. Miyazaki will be challenging for her first-ever Finals title.

The women's singles field includes An Se-young, Yamaguchi, and Miyazaki, along with P.V. Sindhu (India), Wang Zhiyi, and Chen Yufei (both from China). The remaining two spots were taken by Ratchanok Intanon and Supanida Katethong of Thailand.

TBS described the event as "a tournament where world powerhouses gather, including Paris Olympic gold medalist An Se-young (South Korea) and Chinese players." Wang Zhiyi and Chen Yufei, representing host nation China, were grouped together and mentioned as "Chinese players," while An Se-young was introduced separately with a note on her Olympic gold medal achievement. This detail highlights the stature of the badminton queen.

For Japanese players, An Se-young is also an insurmountable wall. In Yamaguchi's case, although she is heading to Hangzhou as the World Tour ranking No. 1, she is on an 11-match losing streak against An Se-young.

The two most recently faced each other in the Korea Open final on the 8th. After dropping the first game, Yamaguchi took the second game 21-15 to level the match. With that victory, An Se-young recorded an 8-match winning streak against Miyazaki.

An Se-young returns to Hangzhou as the defending champion. Last year, she defeated Wang Zhiyi in the final to claim her 11th title of the season. World No. 1 An Se-young has recorded a 71-1 record (98.6% win rate) in 72 matches this season. She swept the women's singles titles at the Asian Championships, the World Championships, and the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, and with her Korea Open victory, she became the first player to achieve 11 titles in consecutive seasons across both men's and women's singles combined.

In Hangzhou, she will challenge for her 12th title of the season and a 60-match winning streak. Currently on a 55-match winning streak, An Se-young will match the women's singles longest winning record (59 matches) set by Indonesian legend Susi Susanti if she wins all three group stage matches and the semifinal. title: American ATP player wins wildcard to the 2027 Australian Open
article_text:
The 2026 ATP and WTA seasons are only just concluding, but many eyes are already turning to the 2027 Australian Open.

That has been particularly true for many lower-ranked American players, who have been battling it out in the tournament's Wildcard Challenge in recent weeks. It is run via an agreement between the United States Tennis Association (USTA) and Tennis Australia.

Claire Liu won the women's Australian Open Wildcard Challenge last week, but her rank will earn her direct entry into the Grand Slam, meaning runner-up Reese Brantmeier takes her place. The men's edition has now just concluded too, and it is youngster Nishesh Basavareddy who has earned himself a wildcard for Melbourne via the Challenge.

After five weeks of competition, ATP number 109 Basavareddy ends the final standings in first place. He claimed top spot after making it to the final of the HPP Open ATP Challenger 125 in Finland, with his 126 points enough to see off Stefan Kozlov in second. Aidan Mayo and Sebastian Gorzny have finished in a tie for third, with Jenson Brooksby in fifth.

Meanwhile, Basavareddy's fellow American Sloane Stephens finished third in the women's Australian Open Wildcard Challenge. A former US Open champion, Stephens was once on track for an Australian Open wildcard, but Brantmeier has earned the wildcard. Malaika Rapolu finished behind Stephens in fourth, with Julieta Pareja completing the top five.

Previous winners of the men's Challenge include John Isner, Steve Johnson, Chris Eubanks and Ryan Harrison. And former women's recipients include Madison Keys, Iva Jovic, Taylor Townsend and CoCo Vandeweghe.

Despite his relatively brief career so far, Basavareddy already has quite the history at Grand Slam level. Having also won the Wildcard Challenge in 2025, the American met none other than legendary figure Novak Djokovic in the first round of that year's Australian Open. And he threatened to pull off a major upset by taking the first set, but Djokovic recovered to beat Basavareddy 4-6, 6-3, 6-4, 6-2.

However, he has since managed to claim an unforgettable major win, with Basavareddy beating Taylor Fritz in the first round of this year's French Open. Ranked 148th at the time, the Roland Garros wildcard secured the first top 10 win of his career against his compatriot.

title: Jodar Surpasses Agassi, Sets Another Record to Cap Remarkable 2026 Season
article_text:
The records keep piling up for Rafael Jodar, even as his 2026 season winds down.

Per the ATP, the 20-year-old Spaniard has added another historic achievement to his growing list of accomplishments in 2026, making the biggest leap into the year-end Top 10 in ATP Rankings history.

Jodar, who began the season at No.165 in the world, finishes it at No.10, having climbed a staggering 155 spots across the 2026 season.

In doing so, he takes a record away from one of the sport’s all-time greats. Eight-time Grand Slam champion Andre Agassi previously held the distinction, having climbed 104 spots from No.110 to No.6 in 1998.

It’s not the first time Jodar has rewritten the record books this year.

The Spaniard had already smashed the record for the shortest period of time between an ATP main draw debut and a Top 10 debut, needing just 287 days to achieve the feat after making his tour-level debut at the Australian Open in January.

And let’s not forget that Jodar was the only teenager to win an ATP title in 2026, claiming his maiden crown on the clay in Marrakech.

A quarterfinal appearance at Roland Garros and a maiden Masters 1000 final in Shanghai were among the other highlights of a sensational rookie campaign that saw Jodar win 45 tour-level matches against 22 losses and qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin.

What will 2027 bring for one of the brightest young talents in men’s tennis? Given the extraordinary pace of Jodar’s ascent, it’s difficult to put a ceiling on what the Spaniard might accomplish in his sophomore season.

There will be plenty to celebrate before the new season gets underway in January.

title: Davis Cup Final 8: Germany and Great Britain Clash for Semifinal Spot
article_text:
The 2026 Davis Cup reaches its end as Germany and Great Britain square off in the quarterfinals of the Final 8 in Bologna. A place in the semifinals against either Austria or Spain is on the line in what promises to be a fiercely contested tie.

World No. 1 Alexander Zverev headlines the German squad as pre-match favorites, but they will face a formidable British side boasting significant depth and world-class doubles pedigree.

Germany punched their ticket to Bologna with a 3-1 victory over Croatia in the second round of qualifying. Zverev proved pivotal by claiming both of his singles rubbers, while the established tandem of Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz delivered in the doubles.

Team captain Michael Kohlmann relies heavily on Zverev at the top of the order, supported by seasoned veterans Jan-Lennard Struff and Yannick Hanfmann. In doubles, the reliable partnership of Krawietz and Puetz provides Germany with one of the most consistent pairings in team tennis.

Great Britain navigated a flawless path to the Final 8, recording back-to-back 4-0 sweeps against Norway and Ecuador. Captain Leon Smith's roster features Arthur Fery, Cameron Norrie, Toby Samuel, Henry Patten, and Neal Skupski.

Fery enters as Britain's leading singles option, complemented by Norrie's extensive top-level experience. The doubles court remains a major weapon for the Brits, with Patten and Skupski offering Grand Slam-caliber credentials. Historically, Germany holds a narrow 6-5 lead in head-to-head Davis Cup meetings, having won their most recent tie 2-1 in 2021.

The quarterfinal clash takes place on Thursday, November 26, at the BolognaFiere Arena, with play scheduled to begin at 4:00 a.m. ET. The match follows the standard best-of-three format, featuring two singles matches followed by a deciding doubles rubber if the score is tied at 1-1.

The opening will pit the lower-ranked singles players against each other, followed by the headline clash between the top seeds, where Zverev is expected to meet Fery. Krawietz and Puetz are slated to face Patten and Skupski in a high-stakes doubles showdown to secure a spot in the final four.

The BolognaFiere Arena hosts the Davis Cup Final 8 from November 24 to 29, serving as the competition's venue for the second consecutive year. Staged on an indoor hard court, the event brings together the eight best nations in the world competing for the prestigious Davis Cup trophy.

title: 'It was ruthless'- GB's Patten on ending top-ranked partnership with Heliovaara
article_text:
Britain's Henry Patten agrees he was "ruthless" in splitting with his doubles partner and close friend Harri Heliovaara, just days after they received the year-end world number one trophy.

Heliovaara and Patten joined forces in 2024 and won Wimbledon together for the second time in July.

In a post on his blog, the Finnish player detailed the disappointment, shock and anger he felt when Patten phoned him with the news.

"I got a lot of stick for calling Harri to tell him," Patten told BBC Sport before Great Britain's Davis Cup quarter-final against Germany.

"I was crumpled over the toilet after the match and Harri, as he often does, had left very quickly to catch a flight back to his family.

"It was ruthless - it was a really difficult decision for me to make for two reasons.

"The first one is we are year-end number ones and we have a great track record together.

"Secondly, me and Harri grew really close during that time. I still consider Harri one of, if not my best friend.

"He's invited to my wedding in the summer. It was probably the first time in my career that I have had to make a decision like that, and I didn't enjoy it."

Patten's new partner will be compatriot Neal Skupski, who says he decided in the space of a "very stressful few hours" to end his pairing with American Christian Harrison.

Patten and Skupski could play their first match as a regular pair against Kevin Krawietz and Tim Putz to decide Britain's quarter-final against Germany on Thursday.

There is little doubt the dust is still settling on a bruising weekend.

"It was a very uncomfortable few hours, but we did speak over the phone for a long time,” Patten continued.

"Obviously I wasn't expecting him to be over the moon about it, and he absolutely has every right to be angry.

"But in that discussion I said I feel like this decision is based on the tennis. I feel that for both of us [it] has stagnated a bit.

"With some time, we'll still remain good friends. That's certainly my hope."

Patten says he has looked up to Skupski for a long time, and enjoys the energy he brings to the court.

He made contact with Ken Skupski, who coaches his brother, last Friday, and did not speak to Neal until he and Harrison had lost in the last four of the ATP Finals the following day.

"It was a very stressful few hours," Skupski recalled.

"After coming off the court, I went to lunch, spoke to [British doubles coach] Louis Cayer, who couldn't really tell me too much as other [British] players are involved.

"It was down to me and my brother to decide what I wanted to do and, at the end of the day, there was only one decision.

"That was the most difficult part - speaking to Christian. We spoke at the hotel, I told him that this opportunity doesn't come along very often to play with another Briton who is a world number one and be able to play Davis Cup and the Olympics in the future.

"So, I think he understood. I don't know if he quite believed me that we hadn't spoken beforehand, but it was two or three hours after the match in which I decided.

"I'm very happy and comfortable with my decision."

The singles in Bologna are likely to feature Arthur Fery and Cameron Norrie and, as British number one, Fery can expect one of the toughest tasks in men's tennis.

The 24-year-old will be up against world number one and two-time Grand Slam champion Alexander Zverev in the second singles match.

Zverev beat Fery in the Wimbledon semi-finals and again at the Vienna Open, with the Briton only winning two games the second time around.

"I've played him a few times already this year, so it's not going to be a completely new thing, which will help me," Fery told BBC Sport earlier in November.

"The serve for me is a challenge because he's close to 2m and I'm on the shorter side of the players out there.

"I struggled to return him, the ball just gets up a lot on me, but I have been working in practice to fight that.

"That's going to serve me not only against Zverev but in general."

Norrie is expected to face Jan-Lennard Struff in the first singles.

The German reached the quarter-finals of Wimbledon and, at 39 in the world, is currently 13 places above Norrie.

Norrie needs little motivation, but the fact Leon Smith is in his last week as captain after over 16 years in the role may help a little.

“I'm so grateful to be here and I think it adds a little bit of motivation to have Leon in our corner. I want to leave it all out there for him,” Norrie added.

“I really like playing with him on the bench there, I feel very relaxed, very chill, he knows when is the right moment to say something.

"He's a great leader and it's a great honour to be in his team."

title: Wang Zhiyi targets World Tour Finals rematch with Ahn Se-young
article_text:
World No. 3 Wang Zhiyi, 26, of China, is once again challenging the world's top player, Ahn Se-young, 24, of Samsung Life Insurance. After failing to get past Ahn in last year's World Tour Finals championship match, Wang is determined to avenge the loss while in good health.

Singapore's Lianhe Zaobao reported on the 24th, Korea time, that "China's Wang Zhiyi hopes to reach the World Tour Finals final once again," adding: "Wang, who is ranked No. 3 in both the world and World Tour rankings, secured her place in the event early. But she only began looking ahead to the World Tour Finals after winning her second straight Hong Kong Open women's singles title."

The outlet added: "Wang Zhiyi lost 1-2 to South Korea's top star, Ahn Se-young, in last year's final and missed out on the title. She plans to work toward another matchup with the women's singles 'monster' this year."

Wang Zhiyi won the women's singles title at the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Hong Kong Open (Super 500), which ended on the 22nd. She beat Thailand's Pornpawee Chochuwong, ranked No. 8 in the world, 2-0 (21-16, 21-11) in the final to win the tournament for a second consecutive year.

It was her first taste of victory in eight months. Wang Zhiyi had not lifted a trophy since beating Ahn Se-young 2-0 in the All England Open final in March. She also lost repeatedly to Japan's Akane Yamaguchi, dropping to No. 3 in the world rankings.

Although Ahn Se-young did not compete, Wang Zhiyi swept the Hong Kong Open without dropping a game from her first match through the final. The win has given Wang a confidence boost ahead of the World Tour Finals, the season's final tournament.

Wang Zhiyi told Lianhe Zaobao in an interview: "I'm really looking forward to it. The World Tour Finals brings together the eight best players in the world this year. I believe every match will be very competitive and exciting. I hope I can play well, too."

Wang Zhiyi also spoke candidly about the physical problems she has faced. "To be honest, I had a few minor setbacks in previous tournaments. I had leg cramps and diarrhea at the world championships, and before that I had a back problem," she said. "They weren't very serious injuries, but they affected me to some extent. So I hope I can compete at the World Tour Finals in relatively good health."

Wang Zhiyi's biggest challenge is to get past Ahn Se-young. Wang pushed Ahn hard in last year's World Tour Finals final in Hangzhou, China, but ultimately lost 1-2 and surrendered the title on home soil.

Ahn Se-young remains a formidable obstacle this year. Wang Zhiyi lost to Ahn in the semifinals of the 2026 World Championships and settled for bronze. Wang is the only player to have beaten Ahn, who has a 71-1 record this season, but has also admitted she does not know how to beat Ahn.

After winning the Hong Kong Open, Wang Zhiyi was asked by Agence France-Presse how she could beat Ahn Se-young. "Goodness. I don't know either," she replied. "Ahn is very consistent, makes no mistakes and keeps her level of play steady. That makes her hard to beat."

Ahn Se-young is also chasing another milestone in badminton history at this World Tour Finals. After winning 11 titles in each of the past two years, she would become the first player in badminton history, in either singles discipline, to win 12 titles in a single season if she reaches the top of the podium one more time.

The Badminton World Federation (BWF) is also watching Ahn Se-young's pursuit of the record. The BWF said on its official website: "World champion Ahn is one title away from setting a record of 12 wins in a single season, the most ever. Ahn has been the standout player on the World Tour."

Eight Asian players will compete in women's singles at the World Tour Finals, scheduled for Dec. 9-13 in Hangzhou, China. South Korea's Ahn Se-young will vie for the title alongside Akane Yamaguchi and Tomoka Miyazaki of Japan; Wang Zhiyi and Chen Yufei of China; Pusarla Venkata Sindhu of India; and Ratchanok Intanon and Pornpawee Chochuwong of Thailand.

Unlike in the world rankings, Yamaguchi will be the No. 1 seed at the World Tour Finals, with Ahn Se-young seeded No. 2. Wang Zhiyi will be the No. 3 seed. Because the top two seeds will be placed in different groups, Ahn will not face Yamaguchi in the group stage. Depending on the draw, however, she could meet Wang in the group stage.<
