title: Arthur Fery backed to 'take risks and enjoy' Carlos Alcaraz clash at Davis Cup
article_text:
Leon Smith has told Arthur Fery to have no regrets if he gets the chance to play Carlos Alcaraz in the Davis Cup semi-finals.

Great Britain's upset win over Germany in Bologna on Thursday set up a mouth-watering clash with Spain as Smith's side bid to reach the final for the first time since claiming the title in 2015.

Fery will be playing just his fourth match in the competition but is set to face the world No 1 and No 3 back-to-back after losing to Alexander Zverev on Thursday.

Alcaraz sat out Spain's quarter-final win over Austria having won the ATP Finals last weekend despite nursing knee and hamstring issues, but it would be a surprise if he did not play singles - and potentially doubles - on Saturday.

Spain captain David Ferrer was keeping his cards close to his chest, saying: "I will see on Saturday. I don't know yet. But it could be possible."

Mixing in such circles is another indication of Fery's meteoric rise this season, and he was clearly disappointed not to be able to threaten Zverev.

Smith said: "I think it's another chance for him to go out and see what it feels like, then figure out ways that he can actually hurt Carlos.

"The more matches he gets at this level, which is still very, very new for him - I think embrace it, don't be scared of it.

"People hate hearing this 'free hit' thing. It kind of is. Just go out, express yourself. Don't come off the court with any regrets. Try to play safe in any way? No. Go and play. Go and take some risks. Shot make. Enjoy it."

Fery has not taken a set off Zverev in three meetings but this will be his first chance to test himself against Alcaraz, who is on a 14-match winning streak.

Speaking of the prospect, he said: "It would definitely be a massive challenge again.

"I think it would be a different style of play. That might help me. Also having had one match on that court in front of a lot of people against a top, top player, it would probably be good to have a second match on there and that would help me having that experience."

The tie is a rematch of Britain's last semi-final in the competition in Madrid in 2019, where a thrilling deciding doubles ended with Jamie Murray and Neal Skupski losing out to Rafael Nadal and Feliciano Lopez.

Skupski is the only remaining member of that team, and he will be looking to turn the tables if it comes down to the doubles again having produced a notable win alongside Henry Patten against German duo Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz.

Another factor is the British team's desire to finish on a high for Smith, whose tenure of nearly 17 years as captain will end after this week.

Spain are the favourites to win their first title since 2019 and are the only team with two top-10 singles players in Alcaraz and Rafael Jodar.

British No 2 Cameron Norrie claimed an impressive win over Jan-Lennard Struff on Thursday but has lost both his meetings with Jodar comfortably.

Is Wyndham Clark signing with PING? | Special Tour Report
article_text:
If you grew up with golf on TV over Thanksgiving weekend, the Skins Game probably rings a bell. It started in 1983 at Desert Highlands in Scottsdale, Arizona, with about as big a foursome as golf could put together: Jack Nicklaus, Arnold Palmer, Gary Player and Tom Watson.

The rules are simple. Every hole is worth money, and when nobody wins a hole outright, the money rolls over to the next. Fred Couples won it so often he got the nickname “Mr. Skins.” The event disappeared after 2008, then came back on Black Friday last year. This year’s foursome is all new. Brooks Koepka is a five-time major champion trying to get back on track after leaving LIV. Two-time PGA Championship winner Justin Thomas is bringing his comedy back to our screens, Wyndham Clark is coming off a season where he’s been debated as the player of the year, and Jackson Koivun is a 21-year-old rookie who beat Scottie Scheffler to win the 3M Open just a few months ago. They’re playing for $4 million at Atlantic Fields Club in Hobe Sound, Florida.

One big drive can swing a skin and win a pile of money, so here’s a look at what each guy is swinging off the tee.

Koepka has never been loyal to one driver brand. He’s gone from TaylorMade to Srixon, back to TaylorMade in recent years. At the 2025 Masters he picked up a Titleist GT3, his first Titleist driver since 2012, and he’s stuck with it ever since. It’s set at 10 degrees of loft, and is built for strong players who like to shape the ball. He’s still using the same Diamana D+ Limited that’s suited him for quite some time to aid in that performance comfort. That fits Koepka, who loves hitting a big, powerful fade.

Koepka’s first year back on the PGA Tour didn’t go the way he wanted. He played 16 events, made 11 cuts and had just one top 10. That came at the Cognizant Classic in March, near his home in South Florida, where he closed with a 65 and tied for ninth. He also tied for 12th at the Masters and made the cut in three of the four majors.

Koepka called his own season “pretty pathetic” after he missed the FedEx Cup Playoffs, and his driving accuracy was a problem early in the year. So keep an eye on him Friday.

Thomas is a Titleist guy through and through. When Titleist releases a new driver, he’s usually one of the first to try it. This year that’s the GTS2 which he started using at the Masters in April. That was only a month after he returned from back surgery from late 2025.

His last driver change made a big difference. In 2025 he moved into the GT2, the model before the GTS2, after struggling off the tee. That spring he won the RBC Heritage in a playoff, his first win in almost three years. By June he had six top 10s and three runner-up finishes.

The GTS2 hasn’t won him a tournament yet, but it’s helping. Thomas is hitting it about four yards longer than last year and finding more fairways.

Wyndham Clark: TaylorMade Qi4D for a historic season, is PING next?

Clark had a season to remember with a TaylorMade Qi4D driver. He won the CJ Cup in May, his second U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills in June and the BMW Championship in August. Most golfers would put that driver in a glass case and never let anyone touch it. It appears Clark is taking a different approach; having stepped up to the 1st tee with what appears to be a new G450 LST. It looks like he’s still rocking the Project X TITAN Yellow, too.

PING has a new driver coming, the G450, and Tour players have just started getting their hands on it. PING hasn’t officially said much about it, but Clark seems like a natural guy for the low-spin G450 LST. He hasn’t had an equipment contract all year, so he can play whatever he likes, and he already has plenty of PING in the bag: two PING fairway woods and a PING putter, and most recently a set of i240 irons in Mexico. He even started 2026 with a PING driver. I can’t quite make out a clear shot on the wedges but if his experience has been anything like mine, I’m sure they’ve tested the s259 wedges as well.

It’s no secret that Clark loves to tinker. He went through four drivers early this season before he settled on the Qi4D. So when I saw him on the big screen today with the PING in his hand and a new logo on the side of his hat, I started to make some assumptions. Nothing is official yet, but it looks like the putter-only contract with PING is about to turn into a much larger deal.

Being a free agent certainly has perks, but there’s also a lot of benefit in having a specific equipment truck to rely on week in and week out on Tour. I’ve seen Clark interacting with the PING staff a handful of times, and it seems to be a place where he feels really comfortable. This possible signing could be more than just about the money or the clubs, there’s a good chance it’s who he trusts with his career.

Equiti Group Named Official Fintech Partner of 2026 Emirates Dubai 7s
article_text:
Equiti Group has secured the role of Official Fintech Partner for the 2026 Emirates Dubai 7s, deepening its presence in the UAE’s sports and entertainment sector. For fintech professionals, the move highlights a growing trend of regional brokerages leveraging high-traffic cultural events to bridge the gap between complex financial services and mass-market consumer engagement.

The partnership positions Equiti Group as a primary sponsor for the 2026 edition of the Emirates Dubai 7s, scheduled to take place at The Sevens Stadium from 27 to 29 November 2026. The event serves as the opening for the 2026/27 HSBC SVNS season and features 28 international men’s and women’s rugby sevens teams competing across the HSBC SVNS and HSBC SVNS 3 tiers. Following a 2025 event that attracted over 88,000 attendees, the 2026 festival will include rugby, padel, fitness competitions, and the festival's first Gaelic football tournament.

Equiti’s involvement includes pitchside branding and digital screen visibility throughout the venue. In the Festival Village, the fintech will host a co-branded pop-up basketball court in collaboration with Dubai Basketball, offering free play to attendees. The company is also promoting its "Yalla Club," a free fan community designed to drive engagement through basketball shoot-out competitions and prize giveaways, including jerseys signed by Dubai Basketball players. This strategy aims to mirror the fast-paced nature of rugby sevens—a format characterized by two seven-minute halves—with accessible financial technology and habit-building tools.

"We are proud to partner with the 2026 Emirates Dubai 7s, a pinnacle event on the UAE sporting calendar that brings elite international sport and community passion together under one roof. At Equiti, we believe in backing sport at every level and showing up where fans connect, making this iconic festival a natural fit for our values."

Equiti Group is a global fintech firm headquartered in Dubai that has evolved from a regional brokerage into a multi-asset financial services provider. Recently named a UAE Superbrand for 2025, the group operates across several international markets, providing technology-driven market access. The firm has established a significant footprint in the Middle Eastern sports ecosystem; it is a Founding Partner of Dubai Basketball, a front-of-shirt sponsor for Al Wahda FC, and the title sponsor of Dubai’s Youth Football League.

The Emirates Dubai 7s is the Middle East’s largest sports and entertainment festival. It is a cornerstone of the global rugby sevens circuit, a high-speed variant of rugby union that gained significant international visibility following its Olympic debut in 2016. The festival combines elite professional competition with grassroots sports, attracting a diverse demographic of international tourists and local residents. By partnering with a fintech entity, the festival continues to diversify its commercial portfolio beyond traditional beverage and travel sponsors, reflecting the UAE's status as a global hub for financial innovation.

FF News has closely followed Equiti Group’s aggressive expansion and technical integration strategy. In late 2026, the firm moved to partner with Botim to streamline trading account funding for UAE users. This followed a significant technical upgrade where the group integrated TradingView to enhance its multi-asset CFD offering. Beyond software, Equiti has focused on infrastructure and brand visibility, launching an AI-powered technology hub in India and expanding its front-of-shirt sponsorship with Al Wahda FC for the 2026/27 season.

This partnership signals a shift in how fintech firms approach customer acquisition in the Middle East. Rather than relying solely on digital performance marketing, firms like Equiti are moving into "lifestyle fintech," embedding their brands into high-energy physical events to build trust and community. This puts pressure on traditional retail banks and older brokerages that have historically been slow to engage with younger, sports-focused demographics. The challenge for the sector remains whether these high-visibility sponsorships can convert festival-goers into long-term active traders, or if the "fan community" approach serves primarily as a brand awareness exercise in an increasingly crowded UAE financial market.

Equiti Group has become the Official Fintech Partner of the 2026 Emirates Dubai 7s. The partnership brings together a global fintech headquartered in Dubai and the Middle East's largest sports and entertainment festival around a shared belief: world-class experiences should bring more people into the action.

Rugby sevens is the fast-paced, seven-a-side format of rugby union that made its Olympic debut at Rio 2016. Teams play two seven-minute halves on a full-size pitch, with more space to attack than in the 15-a-side game. A single turnover can take a team from defending its own try line to racing towards the other end in seconds.

Emirates Dubai 7s brings world-class rugby to Dubai while giving grassroots teams a place alongside the international sides. Equiti brings that same mindset to finance, using technology to broaden market access without compromising quality and helping people build stronger financial habits.

Under the agreement, Equiti will feature pitchside and on screens across the venue. In the Festival Village, Equiti and Dubai Basketball will bring their co-branded pop-up court, where friends and families can play for free between matches. Fans can join Yalla Club, Equiti's free fan community, to enter a basketball shoot-out for a chance to win prizes from the Equiti tuk tuk. Equiti will also give away jerseys signed by Dubai Basketball players.

"We are proud to partner with the 2026 Emirates Dubai 7s, a pinnacle event on the UAE sporting calendar that brings elite international sport and community passion together under one roof. At Equiti, we believe in backing sport at every level and showing up where fans connect, making this iconic festival a natural fit for our values." - Chantelle Johnson, Equiti CMO.

Jack Draper’s ex-coach tipped to replace Leon Smith as Britain’s Davis Cup captain
article_text:
Great Britain secured a hugely impressive victory in the Davis Cup yesterday, defeating Alexander Zverev’s Germany to reach the semi-finals.

It is the first time they have reached this stage in seven years, and they will now face the unenviable task of trying to topple a stacked Spain side led by Carlos Alcaraz.

Regardless of what happens from here, it has been a fine campaign from Smith’s men, who have done him proud in what will be his final year as captain of the team.

And, whilst his tenure is not officially over just yet, the Scotsman’s successor has already been predicted by journalist Russell Fuller and former Davis Cup star Kyle Edmund.

Speaking on BBC 5 Live just last night, it was Fuller who began, insisting that there is one outstanding option to take over from Smith.

“I think there is one obvious candidate,” he began, prefacing his claim by noting that there remain many former players who also have strong claims.

How would you rate the 2026 WTA and ATP seasons out of 10?

However, Fuller then settled by stating: “I am pretty sure that the LTA are going to decide to go for James Trotman.

“He has a lower profile, but he’s currently Leon Smith’s lead Davis Cup coach; he coached Jack Draper to the top four in the world and the US Open semi-finals and the Indian Wells title. I think that relationship with Draper could be crucial, because if Jack Draper can get fit again next season and is able to return to being a top 10 player once again, then getting him to commit to Davis Cup on a regular basis will be vital to Britain’s chances over the next few years.”

Reacting to this prediction was Edmund, who outlined his excitement at the prospect, whilst also sharing one potential reservation over the potential appointment.

He claimed: “It’s a really interesting one. I don’t doubt that James Trotman could do an amazing job because he is inside the system; he is at the LTA, he knows the players and the players know him as well. Ultimately, they know what he is about, and they trust him.

“The only thing that would be different from a Davis Cup captain point of view is if Trots wants to deal with the media side of things, or the political side, where he has been a coach behind the player, and now he has got to be in front of everyone and lead the team.

“If that is something that he wants to do, then that would make a lot of sense, because he has that relationship with Jack.

“I spent a few years working with Trots as well, and he is a really world-class coach. He knows the game; he is very clever and smart, and it’s almost that next generation with Arthur and Jack coming through. We have always had very good doubles players, so it would be a very smart choice.

“The great thing is that I think, as Great Britain, we have options with past players like Andy, Jamie, and I know Greg would want to do it. I did junior Davis Cup with Greg as well, and he is very passionate about supporting the players.

“Either way, I think there is some really good options there for the team.”

What did Jack Draper achieve with James Trotman as his coach?

If Jack Draper were to get back to full fitness, he would likely revel in the opportunity to work with Trotman again, given all they accomplished as a player-coach partnership.

And, this coach’s ability to nurture young talent and get them to perform to the best of their abilities at the highest level would surely make him a good fit for Davis Cup duties.

Trotman began working with Jack Draper in 2021, guiding the Brit from outside the world’s top 250 to world number four.

During that period, they won three ATP titles, with Stuttgart and Vienna making way for his ultimate accomplishment: winning Indian Wells in 2025.

However, in October of last year, Trotman decided to step back, opting to prioritise family life and return to his role as an LTA men’s national coach.

title: BMW Australian PGA Championship: Cameron Smith in contention in his first DP World Tour event since LIV Golf collapse
article_text:
Former Open champion Cameron Smith roared into contention in his first DP World Tour event since the collapse of LIV Golf with a second round eight-under par in Sydney.

Smith is playing in the Tour under a specific agreement, but made a slow start on day one of the BMW Australian PGA Championship with an opening round 71.

However, an eagle at the 14th by the 33-year-old in his second round helped him reach nine-under at the halfway mark to sit four off leader Nicolai von Dellingshausen ahead of the weekend.

Two birdies in the first three holes ensured Smith made a strong start and he got through his front nine at four-under.

A bogey at the 10th provided a setback, but the 2022 Open champion regrouped to get the shot back at the 11th before a superb approach helped Smith set up an eagle opportunity.

After he landed the eagle on the 14th, birdies on the 16th and 17th wrapped up a fine round of 64.

"It's only Friday, so we've still got a couple days to go, but it's nice to play the weekend," Smith said.

"It's nice to be in a position where I can compete and that's where I need to be to make my game better is competing and being under the pump a little bit. I kind of got in a bit of a groove and a bit of a rhythm today."

Northern Irishman Tom McKibbin is one shot ahead of Smith on 10-under after he hit 65 at The Lakes Golf Club on Friday.

Von Dellingshausen matched Smith with 64 to hold a three-shot lead on 13-under, but almost produced a hole-in-one at the 15th.

Later in the day, Robbie Minns did claim a hole-in-one with a seven iron at the 18th to win a BMW X5 40i.

Three players are tied for fourth on seven-under and England's Sam Bairstow is joint 18th on four-under after a second round score of 69.

title: Son of major champion and former LIV Golf pro headline entries to PGA Tour Q-School
article_text:
Several notables are heading to qualifying school next month with hopes of earning a coveted PGA Tour card for the 2027 season.

Often called the most nerve-wracking exam in golf, Qualifying School - or Q-School - is an annual tournament series offering a direct route onto the world's premier men's circuit.

Unlike standard events, it is purely about survival. It offers a vital lifeline for fading stars, rising amateurs and tour journeymen.

However, just five cards are up for grabs.

Players enter at different points depending on their world ranking and past achievements.

- Pre-Qualifying: 54 holes across eight sites (completed in September/October).

- First Stage: 72 holes across 14 sites (completed in October/November).

- Second Stage: 72 holes across five sites (1–4 December).

- Final Stage: 72 holes at Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida (10–13 December).

A set percentage of players advance from each site.

At Final Stage, competitors play two rounds each on the Dye's Valley Course at TPC Sawgrass - home of the Players Championship - and Sawgrass Country Club.

Only the top five finishers at Final Stage earn full PGA Tour membership.

Any tie for fifth is settled by a sudden-death play-off.

- Final Stage (6th–45th and ties): Earn Korn Ferry Tour cards with varying early-season exemptions.

- Final Stage (Remaining finishers): Receive conditional Korn Ferry Tour and PGA Tour Americas status.

- Second Stage medallists: Secure conditional Korn Ferry Tour membership.

- First Stage medallists: Earn PGA Tour Americas status.

Next week's Second Stage features a fascinating mix of former champions, cult heroes and emerging prospects.

Scotland's Russell Knox, a two-time PGA Tour winner, is trying to reclaim his card at the age 41.

He tees off at Hammock Beach in Florida alongside American Jeff Overton, fondly remembered for his wild celebrations at the 2010 Ryder Cup alongside Bubba Watson.

In California, big-hitting three-time winner Cameron Champ is battling a five-year winless slump after finishing 207th in the FedEx Cup.

Joining him at Valencia Country Club is South Korea's Sang-moon Bae, whose career stalled after mandatory military service in 2015.

John Daly II, the son of former Open champion John Daly, is teeing it up at Highland Oaks in Alabama.

And finally, former LIV Golf player James Piot continues his bid to try and earn a route back to the PGA Tour.

title: How Justin Thomas’ criticism of Bryson DeChambeau made the PGA Tour change their rules
article_text:
Bryson DeChambeau has always been a rather deliberate golfer, and that's putting it kindly.

The truth of the matter is that he is one of the slowest golfers in the game.

In fairness, Justin Thomas isn't quick either, and he has actually suggested in the past that he plays far too slowly.

However, Thomas took offence at DeChambeau's pace of play seven years ago during a PGA Tour event.

If Thomas thinks you're slow, you obviously have a problem with the speed with which you play the game.

Things came to a head back in 2019 and the PGA Tour were forced to act after something Thomas said about his fellow American.

After the Northern Trust in 2019, the PGA Tour began to explore a new policy, whereby they could start addressing players' pace of play whose groups were actually in position, but who take an excessive amount of time to hit a shot.

The reason the PGA Tour began exploring that possibility may well have been because of something that Justin Thomas said.

After playing alongside DeChambeau at the Northern Trust in 2019, the two-time PGA Championship winner shared his frustrations at his fellow American's pace of play.

"I like Bryson as a person, but he's a slow golfer," Thomas admitted.

"I hate saying this because I don't want Bryson to think I'm throwing him under the bus or anything like that, but it's just unfortunate where the pace of play is in the game at the moment."

Of course, the PGA Tour now closely monitor players' pace of play, even if they are keeping up with the group in front of them.

The concerning thing for professional golf is that the slow play problem has got even worse over the past few years.

Rounds at the US Open over the past two years were taking over six hours at times, and that is simply unacceptable.

Something needs to be done about the problem as a matter of urgency. Whether that be introducing shot clocks or limiting the size of fields, something needs to change because young fans of the game will be put off immediately by a sport which takes five or six hours to play at a time.

title: BWF bans Thai badminton player Pink Pitchamon for 3 months over banned substance
article_text:
BANGKOK — 27 November 2026, The Badminton World Federation (BWF) confirmed a three-month ban for Thai women’s singles player Pitchamon Opatniputh, known as Pink, after the banned substance furosemide was found in her test at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, in September.

Pitchamon, the 2023 world junior champion, had earlier been provisionally suspended. She missed the Asian Games for Thailand.

Furosemide is a diuretic, sometimes called a “water pill,” used to treat fluid retention and high blood pressure. It is prohibited in sport because it can mask the use of other banned substances or cause rapid weight loss through fluid loss.

The BWF said the anti-doping rule violation process has finished. The three-month ban is counted from the date she was provisionally suspended.

The ban ends on 20 December 2026, and she can return to competition from 21 December.

title: Sesame becomes the new Main Sponsor of Levante UD
article_text:
The leading comprehensive platform in talent and human resources management supports the club for the entire season.

Levante UD and Sesame, the leading comprehensive platform for talent and human resources management, have reached a sponsorship agreement through which the Valencian technology company becomes the Main Sponsor of the club starting from the 2026/27 season.

As the main sponsor of the men's first team, Sesame will feature on the front of the official game jersey as we already saw a few days ago with the launch of the first and second kits, on training gear, and on other physical and digital assets of the club. The agreement also includes a comprehensive program of activations, VIP experiences, corporate events, and content initiatives that will bring the brand closer to fans and the business community.

For Sesame, this sponsorship represents a key step in its brand positioning and visibility, associating itself with one of the historic clubs of Spanish football and a benchmark in Valencian sports. Additionally, this agreement reflects a growing trend in which high-growth technology companies seek to connect their brands with spaces capable of generating community, belonging, and shared emotions. For the company, football represents an environment where values such as teamwork, perseverance, and talent development are experienced every day.

“This alliance with Levante UD makes perfect sense for us. Football and scale-ups like Sesame have much more in common than it seems. Both of us thrive on building teams, developing talent, making quick decisions, and competing every day to improve. At Sesame, we believe that this way of understanding growth deserves to go beyond offices and connect with millions of people,” stated Albert Soriano, CEO of Sesame.

The head of Sesame also emphasized the local nature of the collaboration. “We are especially excited that this agreement is with a club from our homeland. We are a tech company born in Valencia that now works with companies all over the world, and we are very proud of our origins as well as being able to support Levante UD,” added Soriano.

For Levante UD, it is a great satisfaction to be associated with and display on their chest the brand of a Valencian technology company that is a leader in the field of human resources. “The arrival of Sesame as the main sponsor reinforces our commitment to innovation, professionalism, and continuing to grow hand in hand with companies that are transforming their sectors from Valencia to the world,” stated Pablo Sánchez, president of Levante UD.

Following the announcement of this agreement, Sesame and Levante UD are opening a new phase of collaboration in which various joint actions are planned, as well as the promotion of projects that go beyond sports sponsorship, bringing innovation, technology, sports, and the values of talent closer to Levante fans and society as a whole.

Sesame is human resources software focused on redefining the employee experience. It allows the digitalization of the most routine human resources processes so that managers and HR professionals can focus on talent, professional development, and the well-being of their teams, thereby growing their business and building a successful corporate culture. Currently, they have more than 20,000 clients in over 30 countries across Europe and Latin America.

Argentina bans online betting by minors, gambling sponsorships
article_text:
Argentina's Senate has unanimously passed legislation banning minors from online gambling and prohibiting betting companies from advertising, promoting or sponsoring gambling on sports kits, a move aimed at tackling gambling addiction among young people.

The bill passed with 72 votes in favour, both in the general vote and on individual articles, following an agreement between the ruling La Libertad Avanza (LLA) party and the Peronist opposition.

The legislation had been stalled for more than two years and was close to losing parliamentary status before renewed pressure from the Catholic Church. The recent visit by Pope Leo XIV to Argentina helped bring it back to the agenda.

President Javier government had sought to approve an amended version of the bill focused on combating illegal gambling, but opposed sweeping restrictions on advertising, a position also backed by the Argentine Football Association (AFA) and several top clubs that receive large amounts of sponsorship money from betting companies.

The law's central provisions prevent minors from betting on digital platforms and prohibit advertising, promotion and sponsorship of gambling and online betting.

The restrictions extend to the Internet, social media, information and communications technology, audiovisual media and outdoor advertising.

Betting company sponsorship of sports kits is also banned, as is advertising in print, radio, television and other existing or future communications platforms.

Advertising will only be permitted inside casinos, bingo halls, racecourses, betting venues and lottery agencies.

The legislation also establishes prison sentences of between three and eight years for those who organise or operate gambling systems without authorisation from the relevant jurisdiction.

It introduces a series of preventive measures, including a self-exclusion register, identity checks using facial recognition, restrictions on payment methods and alerts notifying users of the time and money they spend gambling.

One of the bill's sponsors, ruling La Libertad Avanza party lawmaker Agustín Coto, said: "If we pass this law today, I want people to understand that we are not here to morally police anyone. This is not about who is good or bad, but about public health. There is a limit, and that limit is children."

Catamarca Peronist Senator Lucía Corpacci said the public was demanding an urgent response, describing the legislation as the most comprehensive of the bills they had introduced on the issue.

"We need to pass this law. Although the provinces regulate gambling, we are now talking about a different kind of game," she said.

She warned that online betting had become part of everyday life for many minors, who gamble from their living rooms, bedrooms and even schools.

"We are talking about gambling from the living room of a house, from a child's bedroom or even from school, because online betting is part of the everyday reality of many minors who gamble at school," she added.

Ruling party Senate leader Patricia Bullrich shared the testimony of the mother of a 26-year-old man who had reached breaking point because of gambling addiction and debts.

"No child or family can keep waiting for the pace of politics. This law must be passed today," she wrote in a post on social media.

Closing the debate, Peronist bloc leader José Mayans welcomed the agreement between the parties and said passing the bill unanimously would be a positive signal.

"I think it is very good that we can pass this unanimously," he said, praising Congress for taking up the issue again, rather than allowing it to be postponed once more.

Bullrich even proposed naming the legislation the "Pope Leo XIV Law" in recognition of the impetus the issue had received, though she stressed that families and schools have a role in tackling gambling addiction.

Church leaders welcomed the bill's passage in a statement, writing: "This achievement does not belong to any particular sector: it is a collective triumph for all of Argentine society.”

The law will force the domestic football authorities to rip up its commercial arrangements, with clubs including Boca Juniors and River Plate set to face large financial blows.

The restrictions cover betting company logos on shirts as well as advertising at stadiums, in public spaces and on clubs' social media channels.

Boca and River both have betting sponsors on their official club kits, while the AFA and domestic top flight will also have to adapt their commercial agreements and advertising.

Although Argentina's national team does not wear betting company sponsors on its shirts, such brands feature across its digital channels, press conference banners and television advertising.

Betting companies are among the main shirt sponsors of clubs including Boca, River, Independiente, Racing, San Lorenzo, Huracán, Rosario Central and Newell's, among other clubs.

Boca and River have the two biggest betting sponsorship deals in Argentine football, both running until 2028, which will have to be renegotiated.

The restrictions will also extend to footballers, coaches, former players, referees, sports journalists and influencers, who will no longer be allowed to feature in betting advertising campaigns, promote sites or share promotional codes through media or social networks.

Many national team stars, including goalkeeper Emiliano 'Dibu' Martínez, have advertised betting firms.

Broadcasters showing matches in the Primera División and lower divisions will also have to remove betting adverts during games and from their regular programming.

title: DOJ probing NFL over potential antitrust violations in TV deals, sources say - ABC News
article_text:
It's said to involve whether customers are forced to pay more for subscriptions.

The Justice Department has opened an inquiry into whether the National Football League violated anticompetitive practices in its TV deals and then required customers to pay too much in subscription costs, according to three sources familiar with the probe.

The Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961 gives some limited protections for the NFL which allows for sports leagues to pool broadcast rights.

"This is about affordability and creating an even playing field for providers," a government official told ABC News.

The Justice Department declined to comment. The Wall Street Journal first reported news of the probe.

In a statement to ABC News, the NFL defended its distribution model.

"The NFL's media distribution model is the most fan and broadcaster-friendly in the entire sports and entertainment industry," it said. "With over 87% of our games on free, broadcast television, including 100% of games in the markets of the competing teams, the NFL has for decades put our fans front and center in how we distribute our content. The 2025 season was our most viewed since 1989 and reflects the strength of the NFL distribution model and its wide availability to all fans."

Sen. Mike Lee, a Utah Republican who has been publicly urging the Justice Department to investigate the NFL's conduct, cheered news of the antitrust probe on his X account.

"Instead of a small number of free broadcast networks, the NFL now licenses games simultaneously to subscription streaming platforms, premium cable networks, and technology companies operating under different business models," he said on X.

"To the extent collectively licensed game packages are placed behind subscription paywalls, these arrangements may no longer align with the statutory concept of sponsored telecasting or the consumer-access rationale underlying the antitrust exemption," he posted.

"That's why, as chair of the Subcommittee on Antitrust, Competition Policy, and Consumer Rights, I urged the DOJ to examine the Sports Broadcasting Act and its applicability to current media landscape. I'm glad they're tackling this," he said.

title: River and Loma Negra: Sponsorship Agreement as Part of the Monumental Expansion and Roofing
article_text:
The leading company in the construction industry became the official sponsor of the Club until 2030, under an agreement that includes the provision of concrete for the expansion and roofing works of the Stadium.

River Plate and Loma Negra announced the signing of a sponsorship agreement through which the cement company will be a strategic supplier for the expansion and roofing works of the Monumental Stadium by providing concrete, thus becoming the official sponsor of the Club until 2030.

The initiative brings together two centenarian Argentine institutions, protagonists of their respective activities and united by a trajectory built on passion, work, and the constant pursuit of excellence. Loma Negra will contribute its experience, technical capacity, and solutions for the construction of an emblematic project for River, its members, and fans.

The agreement includes brand presence in the Club's official spaces and channels, including the Monumental Stadium, River Camp, press conferences, digital content, and social networks. It will also develop activations and experiences aimed at clients and other audiences related to Loma Negra.

Additionally, it foresees pre-match experiences and interactions with the professional squad, visits to training sessions, exclusive tours of the River Museum, corporate events at the Club's facilities, and various actions during local tournament matches.

Stefano Di Carlo stated: “Adding Loma Negra as an Official Sponsor represents a very important step to continue driving the transformation of the Monumental. Their experience and leadership in the construction industry will be fundamental to accompany this new challenge and continue consolidating a stadium prepared to welcome millions of people each year.”

In turn, Sergio Faifman (CEO of Loma Negra) noted: “This project brings together two centenarian institutions, deeply connected with the country and with a history marked by growth, innovation, and the ability to build projects that leave a mark.”

Loma Negra is the leading company in the Argentine cement industry and celebrates 100 years in 2026 as a protagonist in the construction of the country. Since its inception in Olavarría in 1926, the company has developed an integrated business and a wide productive and logistical network that allows it to reach the main markets in Argentina.

It produces and markets cement, masonry cement, lime, concrete, and aggregates, providing solutions for distributors, concrete producers, industrial clients, and large infrastructure projects.

Its trajectory is based on innovation, operational excellence, and the constant pursuit of sustainable solutions. Through its products, services, and technical capacity, Loma Negra supports the development of works that transform communities and contribute to the country's growth.

title: Rabobank becomes new title partner of…
article_text:
From the 2027 season, Rabobank will become the first title partner of Team Visma | Lease a Bike’s women’s team. Led by Marianne Vos and Pauline Ferrand-Prévot, the team will continue as Rabobank | Lease a Bike Women’s Pro Cycling Team. This marks the next step in the partnership that began in 2025. Rabobank takes over from Visma, which will remain involved with the team as a Founding Partner.

The expanded partnership marks the prominent return of the Rabobank name to professional cycling, a sport in which the bank has a long history. Team leaders Marianne Vos and Pauline Ferrand-Prévot, who both spent five years riding for the former Rabobank women’s team, will once again wear a Rabobank jersey from 2027.

The title sponsorship underlines Rabobank’s confidence in the team and its ambition to further grow women’s cycling. Together, Rabobank and the team will develop initiatives to raise the profile of women’s cycling and encourage more girls to take up the sport.

Rabobank and the team share the ambition to strengthen cycling at every level: from introducing children to the sport through initiatives such as the Rabo Dikke Banden Races to developing cycling talent and supporting riders competing at WorldTour level. Rabobank will also remain a Premium Partner of the men’s and development teams, retaining its existing logo positions on their jerseys.

This next step comes at a time when women’s cycling is experiencing significant growth, both in sporting terms and in terms of public and commercial interest. With Dutch and international talent, the women’s team offers Rabobank a powerful platform to contribute to this continued development. The team’s international profile also aligns well with the bank’s ambitions in key European growth markets.

CEO Richard Plugge is proud of this next step in the partnership with Rabobank: “Given our shared history, the return of the Rabobank name as a title partner is a special moment. It demonstrates Rabobank’s confidence in our team and in the future of women’s cycling. We are proud to build on that confidence together.”

Carlo van Kemenade, member of Rabobank’s Managing Board: “When we returned to cycling last year, our ambition was to give the sport a boost, with a focus on elite sport, talent development and grassroots sport in the Netherlands. Our return generated a great deal of positivity and enthusiasm. By taking on a greater role in women’s cycling, we are building on that momentum. This reflects who we are as a cooperative bank and our commitment to local communities. From the first introduction to the sport to competing at the highest level, we want to contribute to a sport in which talent has even more opportunities to flourish. For us, that is the power of investing in sport together.”

title: Visma | Lease a Bike counters Vollering's FDJ with an exclusive women's team sponsorship deal
article_text:
Rabobank is, of course, a well-known name in cycling, although its departure in 2012—due to the troubling doping scandals in the cycling peloton—wasn’t exactly on good terms.

After it also parted ways with the women’s team in 2016, the Dutch bank was absent from the cycling scene for several years. That is, until 2025, when it suddenly began sponsoring teams again.

In July of that year, it returned to Visma | Lease a Bike, initially as a partner of the men’s, women’s, and development teams.

It is also affiliated with the Dutch cycling federation and TeamNL, and organises events such as the Rabo NXT Classic, Ready2Race, and the Rabobank Dikke Banden Races.

Now, it is adding title sponsorship of the Visma | Lease a Bike women’s team to its portfolio.

For the women’s team, Rabobank is, of course, primarily filling a void that opened up after Visma scaled back its role within the organisation, transitioning from title sponsor to founding partner.

However, it also sends an important signal to women’s sports, where an increasing number of major sponsors are committing exclusively to women’s teams, without considering the men’s division.

Demi Vollering’s French team will be renamed TotalEnergies-FDJ United in 2027 and already has a major sponsor on board in Red Bull. As a result, Stephen Delcourt’s team has grown rapidly.

Visma | Lease a Bike has provided more details through official channels about its deal with Rabobank for 2027. The team will be called the 'Rabobank | Lease a Bike Women’s Pro Cycling Team' and represents “the next step in the partnership that began in 2025.”

"The title sponsorship underscores Rabobank's confidence in the team and its ambition to further grow women's cycling. Together, Rabobank and the team are developing initiatives to raise awareness of women’s cycling and encourage more girls to get on their bikes,” the team said.

CEO Richard Plugge calls it “a special moment” and is pleased with the trust placed by the bank. Carlo van Kemenade of Rabobank adds: “Our return sparked a lot of positivity and enthusiasm. By taking on a greater role in women’s cycling, we’re building on that. That aligns with our identity as a cooperative bank and our local commitment to the community.”

David has been working in the sports & cycling industry for 16 years. Covering racing, business and technology, he has worked in communications for cycling companies, teams, and as a journalist. His proudest achievement is winning the first bike race he ever entered. He hasn't won a race since.

We are so excited to share Rabobank will become the first title partner of our women’s team. From 2027, we proudly race as Rabobank | Lease a Bike Women’s Pro Cycling Team.

title: France team: Galthié responds to Rassie's ploy while sharpshooter Ramos returns for Springboks rematch
article_text:
France have been bolstered by key returnees for the grudge Nations Championship final rematch against the Springboks on Sunday at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.

Fabien Galthié has recalled sharpshooter full-back Thomas Ramos for the final with the Toulouse star recovering from injury and having subsequently been recalled for a first cap this month.

He lines up in the number 15 jersey with Théo Attissogbe shifting to the wing while World Rugby Player of the Year nominee Louis Bielle-Biarrey rounds out the back-three.

Attissogbe replaces Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, who has been ruled out through injury after some impressive performances this year earned him a nomination for the World Rugby Breakthrough Player of the Year Award.

The centres remain unchanged yet again with Yoram Moefana combining with Kalvin Gourgues – a combination that has gone untouched throughout November.

Meanwhile, Les Bleus have been further boosted by Matthieu Jalibert’s return at fly-half with the Bordeaux pivot getting his second start this month after returning from his spell on the sidelines last weekend against Argentina. When France last faced the Boks, they were contending with an injury crisis in the number 10 position with captain Antoine Dupont filling the void but Jalibert has eased those woes as he partners the skipper in the halfbacks.

Into the pack and Anthony Jelonch will combine with Cameron Woki and Francois Cros, the latter duo reclaiming their starting roles after being rested against Argentina while the former replaces Gregory Alldritt from the teamsheet that beat South Africa a fortnight ago.

Florian Verhaeghe and Mickaël Guillard are the starting locks for the French while hooker Maxime Lamothe is flanked by tighthead Sipili Falatea and loosehead Jefferson Poirot in the front-row.

Galthié has opted for a 6-2 bench split for the final with Peato Mauvaka named as the replacement hooker, along with props Jean-Baptiste Gros and Régis Montagne. Gros was a doubt throughout the week but has recovered in time to feature on the bench, with Galthié perhaps replying to Rassie Erasmus’ decision to name his strongest scrummaging front-row on the bench too.

Charles Ollivon and Tyler Duguid provide back-row and lock cover along with Oscar Jégou, who also makes a timely return from injury to feature in the team while Maxime Lucu and Emilien Gailleton are named as the replacement backs.

title: Rugby World Cup: Next four hosts confirmed as Spain bids
article_text:
European rugby fans could be spared a 16-year wait for the men's Rugby World Cup to return to the continent after Spain entered the race to host the 2035 tournament.

World Rugby has already confirmed the hosts of its next four men's and women's tournaments, with Australia and the United States sharing hosting duties.

However, Spain's ambitious bid could bring the men's tournament back to Europe for the first time since France hosted in 2023.

Some of football's most iconic stadiums could even be set for a rugby makeover.

World Rugby is looking to expand the sport's global appeal, with the next four tournaments taking place outside Europe.

The 2031 tournament will be the first men's Rugby World Cup staged in the United States, marking a major milestone for the sport.

However, European supporters hoping to watch the men's tournament closer to home must wait until at least 2035.

Spain is no stranger to hosting rugby in front of enormous crowds.

A staggering 99,124 spectators packed into Barcelona's Camp Nou to watch Racing 92 defeat Toulon in the 2016 Top 14 final.

Now, Spain wants to bring the biggest tournament in rugby to its shores.

Barcelona's Camp Nou and Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabéu could provide spectacular backdrops for the competition.

Spain will also be able to build on the infrastructure developed for the 2030 FIFA World Cup, which it will co-host alongside Portugal and Morocco.

The country's national rugby team has already qualified for the 2027 Rugby World Cup, ending a 28-year absence from the tournament.

With England and South Africa opting against submitting bids, Spain faces competition from two rival proposals.

- 🇪🇸 Spain: Looking to host for the first time.

- 🇯🇵 Japan: Hoping to repeat the success of 2019.

- 🌎 South America: A joint bid involving Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Uruguay.

Should Spain's bid prove unsuccessful, Europe would miss out on three successive men's Rugby World Cups.

If Japan or South America wins the race for 2035, European supporters will have to wait until at least 2039.

When will the 2035 Rugby World Cup host be confirmed?

Under World Rugby's host selection process, a preferred host is expected to be identified in May 2027, with the final decision scheduled for November.

Spain offers the opportunity to take rugby's biggest tournament into a new market while bringing it back within easy reach of millions of European supporters.

For now, Spain is flying the flag for an entire continent.

title: Rassie Erasmus six-match ban takes unexpected twist
article_text:
Rassie Erasmus looks increasingly likely to serve his six-match suspension in full after a surprising revelation emerged ahead of Sunday's Nations Championship final.

SA Rugby immediately announced its intention to challenge the punishment handed down by World Rugby earlier this month.

However, despite initially pushing for an expedited hearing, reports suggest the governing body never formally submitted its request.

With the Springboks preparing to face France at Twickenham, RUCK looks at how the disciplinary saga has unfolded.

South Africa suffered a 21-19 defeat to France in the Nations Championship, with several refereeing decisions becoming major talking points following the final whistle.

Speaking at a press conference in Dublin, Erasmus questioned why several incidents of suspected foul play against his players had gone unpunished.

His comments about potential match manipulation attracted the attention of World Rugby.

World Rugby announced that Erasmus had been suspended for six international matches with immediate effect.

The Springboks boss became one of three international rugby coaches banned in the space of just eight days as the governing body continued its crackdown on the mistreatment of match officials.

Erasmus retained the right to request a full misconduct hearing.

Just 20 minutes after the suspension was announced, SA Rugby released a statement signalling its intention to challenge the punishment.

The union wanted Erasmus to explain the context of his remarks and hoped a hearing could be arranged quickly.

With the Ireland Test fast approaching, Erasmus remained suspended.

The Springboks boss served the first match of his suspension as South Africa suffered a 20-17 defeat to Ireland.

Unable to attend the match, Erasmus instead hosted an online watchalong for supporters.

The South African, citing reporting from The Times, revealed that a formal challenge had still not been lodged.

The publication raised the possibility that SA Rugby had quietly accepted the punishment.

Further reporting from The42 indicated that SA Rugby had still not followed through on its public announcement with a formal request for a hearing.

Meanwhile, the Springboks boss could face another disciplinary headache after it emerged that Erasmus could face an even longer ban from World Rugby following comments made during his watchalong.

Ten days after the original suspension was announced, there is still no public confirmation of a hearing.

Erasmus is set to serve the second match of his ban against France on Sunday, leaving four internationals outstanding heading into 2027.

Despite SA Rugby's swift response to the original punishment, the Springboks boss looks increasingly likely to serve his suspension in full.

Neither governing body has officially confirmed that the matter is closed.

title: France boss responds to Springboks and All Blacks doping controversy
article_text:
France head coach Fabien Galthie has expressed his surprise after reports revealed that no random post-match drug tests were carried out during the entire Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour between South Africa and New Zealand.

An investigation by The Times found that none of the eight matches on the tour, which included four provincial fixtures and four Tests, featured random post-match drug testing.

Almost 170 players took part across the series, with New Zealand Rugby confirming that none of its players were tested during the trip.

The South African Institute for Drug-Free Sport (SAIDS), which oversees the testing programme, said its priority was out-of-competition testing.

It insisted that no regulations had been broken, while World Rugby defended its wider anti-doping programme.

The number of tests has fallen by around 70 per cent over the past decade, dropping from 753 in 2015/16 to just 225 in 2025/26.

The revelations come just days before the Springboks face France in the inaugural Nations Championship final. There is, however, no suggestion of wrongdoing by either team during the tour.

Galthie has now given his reaction to the findings, speaking to RMC Sport about the importance of regular testing and fairness in the game.

"This is something very important. Very, very important. In any case, we are very sensitive to it. To the health of the players and to fairness.

"We have been tested three times since November, three times in Marcoussis, three times at 6:30 am, three times four players. We participate very attentively in the tests imposed on us by World Rugby."

The France boss admitted he was particularly surprised by the suggestion that some teams had not been tested throughout the tour.

"I am surprised, very surprised by what you are telling me this morning, that some teams have not been tested. I don't know if it's fair, if it's true. But in any case, we are paying close attention to it. Testing, fairness, it's very important in our sport.

"This is the governing body of world rugby. So the reins belong to World Rugby. Since it's their competition, it's World Rugby that organises fairness and equity within its competition.

"World Rugby is responsible for fairness. I don't know if the information is accurate, but for me it's crucial and very important. We pay close attention to it. We like and want to be audited regularly."

title: Tommaso Menoncello could miss Six Nations after latest injury setback
article_text:
Italy centre Tommaso Menoncello is facing a race against time to be fit for the 2027 Six Nations after suffering another setback in his ongoing shoulder injury.

The 24-year-old initially injured his left shoulder against Exeter in October and spent five weeks on the sidelines. However, after returning to training on Monday, the problem flared up again.

Menoncello is now expected to undergo surgery next week, which could keep him out for three to four months.

The setback is a major blow for Italy, with the 41-cap centre now likely to miss the 2027 Six Nations. He had already been ruled out of the Nations Championship.

Menoncello joined French giants Toulouse ahead of the 2026/27 campaign following six years at Benetton.

He made his international debut against France in the 2022 Six Nations, scoring a try to become the youngest player to score in the tournament's history at just 19.

Since then, he has developed into one of Italy's most important players, earning the 2024 Six Nations Player of the Championship award.

His absence will be another concern for Gonzalo Quesada, whose side face Fiji at Allianz Stadium this afternoon in their final Nations Championship fixture.

Italy have collected just two points from their six summer and autumn matches, despite enjoying an encouraging Six Nations campaign earlier this year. They will be desperate to secure a first-ever victory over Fiji.

Injuries have played a significant part in their difficult run of results. Quesada was without 16 players for Italy's opening autumn fixture against South Africa, with Menoncello among those unavailable.

While the results have been disappointing, the sheer number of absentees has made life particularly difficult for the Italian head coach.

There is also a longer-term concern for Menoncello, with the timing of his recovery potentially affecting his preparations for next year's World Cup.

If he misses the Six Nations, he could go more than a year without playing Test rugby. His last appearance for Italy came against the All Blacks in July.

title: Top stars Mirra Andreeva and Linda Noskova enter the 2027 Porsche Tennis Grand Prix
article_text:
- The 19-year-old youngster Mirra Andreeva won her first Grand Slam title this year at the French Open. She also triumphed at the WTA Finals.

- The year’s breakout player ended the most successful season of her career as the world No. 2.

- Linda Noskova firmly established herself as a top player when winning Wimbledon.

- The long-established Stuttgart tournament will take place in the Porsche Arena from 10 to 18 April 2027.

- Special Christmas ticket offer from 1 to 24 December with a ten per cent discount on selected seats.

For Mirra Andreeva, 2026 marks an important milestone in her still young career. The 19-year-old claimed her first ever Grand Slam title at the French Open to celebrate her biggest sporting success to date. Currently the world No. 2, she additionally won this year’s tournaments in Adelaide and Linz and, most recently the WTA Finals, the season-ending tournament for the eight most successful women players. She was the runner-up in Madrid and Beijing. At the Porsche Tennis Grand Prix, she reached the semifinals.

Linda Noskova also secured her first Grand Slam win of her career in 2026. With her triumph at Wimbledon, the 22-year-old Czech claimed the most prestigious title in tennis. This year, the world No. 7 also won the tournament in Berlin and reached the penultimate round at the WTA Finals. She was also a quarterfinalist at the Porsche Tennis Grand Prix.

“With Mirra and Linda in the line-up, two of the past season’s most successful players have entered early for the Porsche Tennis Grand Prix in April. It’s really pleasing and a good indication of just how important our tournament is amongst the players,” says Tournament Director Markus Günthardt. “Our spectators can already look forward to world class tennis in the Porsche Arena. Our aim is to once again present them with an exceptionally strong field of players in 2027.”

As a part of the traditional special Christmas offer from 1 to 24 December, tennis fans will receive a ten per cent discount on seats from Monday through to Thursday during the tournament week. These and other tickets are available at the www.porsche-tennis.de tournament website as well as at Easy Ticket (www.easyticket.de, telephone +49 711/2 55 55 55). VIP tickets offer a special tennis experience as visitors will be able to watch the top players from right next to the action on Centre-Court and have access to exclusive lounges with a comprehensive range of hospitality services. All the details about VIP tickets, individual group bookings and VIP boxes are available at vip@perfectmatch.de.

First played in 1978, the Porsche Tennis Grand Prix is the flagship of Porsche’s worldwide involvement in women’s tennis. The Stuttgart WTA tournament stands for tradition and innovation, just like the Porsche brand. As the most loyal sponsor of women’s international tennis, the sports car manufacturer has accompanied the WTA’s oldest indoor event right from the start. Porsche has also been a premium partner of the “Deutsche Tennis Bund” (DTB – German Tennis Association) since 2012 and is committed to fostering up-and-coming players in the Porsche Talent Team.

title: Thailand’s Pitchamon Opatniputh handed three-month ban for doping
article_text:
Thailand’s Pitchamon Opatniputh has received a three-month suspension after testing positive for the banned substance furosemide in a test carried out before the recently concluded Asian Games in Japan, the Badminton World Federation (BWF) announced on Friday.

The world governing body confirmed that the anti-doping proceedings against the world No. 22 had concluded, with her suspension backdated to the start of her provisional ban.

Her period of ineligibility will end on December 20, 2026.

“The Badminton World Federation (BWF) can confirm the outcome of the anti-doping case involving Thailand badminton player Pitchamon Opatniputh, following an adverse analytical finding for the prohibited substance furosemide at the Asian Games in September this year,” the BWF said in a statement.

“The matter has now concluded, with a three-month period of ineligibility commencing from her provisional suspension. Her period of ineligibility will expire on 20 December 2026.”

Furosemide, a diuretic, is included in the World Anti-Doping Agency’s (WADA) list of prohibited substances.

The 19-year-old, who won the world junior title in 2023, returned a positive sample during out-of-competition testing in Nagoya, two days before the Asian Games opening ceremony. She was subsequently prohibited from competing, training or taking part in the continental showpiece.

Opatniputh finished runner-up at the Indonesia Masters Super 500 and Orleans Masters Super 300 earlier this year.

The Thai shuttler also has two Super 100 titles to her name, having won in Malaysia in 2023 and at the Baoji China Masters in 2025. She also reached the final of the Taipei Open Super 300 last year.

title: ‘We Requested BWF Not to Downgrade It’: Sehgal on Syed Modi International
article_text:
The Syed Modi India International has been a significant platform for Indian badminton, offering emerging players an opportunity to compete against international opponents on home soil. However, with the tournament set to move from the Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Super 300 category to Super 100 from 2027, questions have emerged over its standing in the international badminton calendar. The organisers, though, are determined to ensure that the tournament continues to serve its purpose.

In an exclusive conversation with RevSportz, Navneet Sehgal, chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Badminton Association (UPBA), revealed that the organisers had requested the BWF not to downgrade the tournament. However, he stressed that its importance would not be defined by its category.

“We have requested them not to degrade it,” Sehgal said. “But anyway, a tournament is a tournament. For us, it gives a lot of opportunity to young and upcoming players. We will not leave any stone unturned in making it a success. Let it be 100 or 300. It is always encouraging for local badminton talent to see top players playing.”

The BWF announced its revamped World Tour structure, under which the Syed Modi International, a Super 300 event since 2018, was moved to the Super 100 category. The decision was part of a wider restructuring of the international circuit, under which India will have fewer tournaments on the World Tour.

Sehgal, however, believes that the tournament’s contribution to the development of Indian badminton should not be measured by its ranking or category.

“I have seen even Super 300 tournaments not attract top players. So it does not make a difference if it is 300 or 100. The tournament standard will be the same. We have put our point across to them, but it is for the BWF to decide,” he added.

The tournament also faced a separate challenge this year when Indian viewers were unable to access the BWF TV YouTube live streams during the opening days because of geo-blocking. The restriction was lifted ahead of Friday’s quarter-finals.

The issue also exposed confusion surrounding domestic broadcast rights. While the BWF clarified that the domestic rights belonged to the Badminton Association of India (BAI), the streaming arrangements initially led to a disagreement over which organisation was responsible for making the coverage available to Indian viewers.

Sehgal said the organisers were initially unaware of the situation and would look at ensuring better coverage in future editions. “We didn’t know about this, otherwise we would have put it on our own YouTube channel,” he said. “We will do it next year. We are putting it live on DD Sports and OTT channel. It will come live from tomorrow onwards.”

Beyond the administrative and broadcast challenges, Sehgal remains optimistic about the growing pool of Indian badminton talent. With 269 players participating in the current edition, including 146 Indians, he believes tournaments like the Syed Modi International provide valuable exposure to players who are still finding their feet at the international level.

The retired IAS officer also highlighted the progress of India’s women’s doubles pair, Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, who have established themselves as one of the country’s leading combinations. Having also watched them win a title in Delhi, Sehgal believes their success reflects the growing strength of Indian doubles badminton.

He also named several young players who could make their mark internationally, including Tanvi Patri, Unnati Hooda and Tanvi Sharma.

“We have got these doubles players coming up now and they are winning many tournaments,” he noted. “We hope a lot of other youngsters come up as well. We have a lot of talent. They will all come up given a chance and an international atmosphere to play. We should have more such players who shine at the international level.”

For Sehgal, the larger objective remains creating opportunities for the next generation rather than worrying about the tournament’s position in the BWF hierarchy. He also shared a message for young players aspiring to reach the highest level.

“Patience is the best thing. Wherever you are, whatever career or sport you choose, you have to keep patience and keep playing. Perseverance and patience are the two things they should have. Whenever they get a chance, they must try to perform to their best,” he concluded.

As the tournament prepares to enter its Super 100 chapter, Sehgal’s focus remains firmly on nurturing India’s next generation of badminton talent.

title: Former Irish Open winner owed money from LIV collapse
article_text:
Former Irish Open winner Lucas Herbert revealed that he was one of a number of former LIV members still owed money from the collapse of the breakaway circuit.

LIV Golf officially came to an end earlier this month after BC Partners Credit opted out of investing further into the league for next year with the disruptor tour being wound up and its assets liquidated.

Herbert, who won the 2021 Irish Open at Mount Juliet, is one of a host of LIV players to have turned his attention to the DP World Tour for 2027 and has signed an agreement to guarantee himself a number of starts alongside eight other players, despite not holding membership of the circuit.

Speaking after missing the cut on home soil at the BMW Australian PGA Championship, Herbert revealed he was still owed money from LIV Golf and he isn’t the only one waiting for his pennies.

“You’re probably foolish to think you’re going to get much of it,” the world No.55 told Fox Sports.

“Anything from this point is going to be a bonus. It’s a long drawn out process with mostly lawyers winning out of the whole battle. I’ve accepted that and moved on. The reality is I made a lot of money at the same time as I’m owed a lot.”

He continued: “As great as a time I had on the LIV tour, I had many legal issues along the way, which drew a lot of energy out of me.

“I’ve played this game a few times now and I’m going to expect not very much and hopefully be pleasantly surprised, rather than the other way around.”

It is not just players who are waiting for their bank accounts to bulge even further, but several businesses and staff haven’t received the money they are owed.

There’s a lot of people who are owed a lot and it means more to them. Catering companies, security companies, event setups, media companies that will potentially go bankrupt.

“People literally can’t pay the bills because of it. I’m not in that position, fortunately. As frustrating as it is, I feel for those people a lot more than asking for sympathy myself.”

With the 2026 season now in the books, players will tackle one of five venues as the second stage of qualifiers take place in the United States.

This year’s hopefuls include a former major champion’s son, PGA Tour winners and more. In no particular order, here they are…

Now 40, the South Korean won twice on the PGA Tour and even represented the International Team in the 2015 Presidents Cup. That was his final event before returning home for mandatory military service.

The big-hitting Californian won three times in his first four seasons on the PGA Tour but is now winless in more than five years and finished outside the top 200 in the FedEx Cup standings.

He became the first US Amateur champion from Michigan in 2021 but after turning pro the following year, Piot has since failed to make his mark.

Among several former PGA Tour winners heading to Q School, Reavie is now 45 and the world No.704. His last victory was in 2022, while he was once ranked 26th in the world.

Who could forget this name? Bennett, the former Texas A&M star, made headlines for his heroics at the 2023 Masters but has drifted out of the public eye in recent years.

Twice a winner on the PGA Tour, in playoffs in 2022 and 2023, List finished 198th in this year’s season-long standings after missing the cut in his last five starts.

The 23-year-old son of former Open champ Daly will bid to earn full playing rights on the PGA Tour for the first time in his career. Daly II made his debut on both the PGA and DP World Tours in 2026.

Into his 40s now, the Scot won some big titles in the height of his career. Knox won a WGC event in 2015 and the Travelers Championship a year later before winning the Irish Open in 2018.

We all remember Overton for his iconic ‘Boom, Baby!’ moment at the 2010 Ryder Cup. The 43-year-old is now trying to win back his card after struggling with health issues for more than a decade. In a recent issue of bunkered, the American opened up on his recovery from a life-threatening infection.
